docs.title: JoSIM - Superconducting Circuit Simulator
docs.text:
User and developer documentation for the current source tree. For published binaries, see GitHub Releases. Fixes and compatibility changes are recorded in the changelog.

The 3.0.0 source line includes the completed branch consolidation and audit repairs. Read compatibility and migration before reusing older results or C++ applications. JoSIM remains freely available under MIT; it is the open-source predecessor of JoSIM-Pro.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
JoSIM was developed under IARPA contract SuperTools(via the U.S. Army Research Office grant W911NF-17-1-0120). JoSIM is a analogue circuit simulator with SPICE syntax input that has inherent support for the superconducting Josephson junction element.

JoSIM is meant to function as an alternative to the simulators such as JSIM1 and WRspice2. JoSIM is written in modern C++ and is fully customizable and extendable to offer support for improved superconducting elements as well better approximations to the Josephson effect in superconducting materials.

A .cir file containing a SPICE syntax circuit netlist is provided as input. The circuit netlist, given appropriate input excitations can then be simulated through transient analysis. Results of this simulation can be dumped to standard output or saved in various formats such as a comma separated value (.csv) file.

Below is a macro overview of the process performed by JoSIM. This is very basic and is discussed in further detail in the Technical Discussion section of the documentation.

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
The JoSIM repository has the following layout. A quick description shows the purpose of the various files and folders.

cmake               # CMake scripts.
docs/
    index.md        # The documentation homepage.
    ...             # Other markdown pages, images and other files.
include/
    JoSIM           # JoSIM header files.
scripts             # Some Python3 scripts to automate testing and plotting
tools               # Build, qualification, sweep and documentation owners.
build/              # Generated builds and documentation (ignored).
artifacts/          # Local qualification results (ignored).
src/
    ...             # JoSIM source files.
test                # Folder containing various examples.
README.md           # Basic readme to get the user going.
LICENSE             # License that governs use of JoSIM.
CMakeLists.txt      # Configuration to compile code.
...                 # Other configuration files and scripts.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Download and extract the archive for your operating system and architecture from GitHub Releases. The executable is in bin/. Add that directory to your PATH, or invoke the executable by its full path. The archive includes the C++ library and headers.

For example, from the repository root with a local build:

build/dev/josim-cli -o build/example.csv test/ex_dcsfq_jtl_sink.cir

On multi-configuration Windows builds the executable is under build/dev/Release/. See Example Usage and the Syntax Guide for netlists, analysis modes and output options.

To compile and test from source, follow Developing JoSIM. The release procedure describes binary targets, runtime baselines and package verification.

Current source additions have separate guides:

  • Gate-controlled junctions
  • Noise sources

docs.title: TimeEx and other tools
docs.text:
Some tools, such as TimEx, require josim-cli to be named josim. Since the josim command line executable (josim-cli) is a singular executable, this means that there are no files that rely on its specific naming for JoSIM to function correctly. It can thus safely be renamed or copies made thereof with varying names as required by external tools (such as TimEx).

Under Unix systems a symbolic link can be established through:

sudo ln -s /usr/local/bin/josim-cli /usr/local/bin/josim

Where the first path is the source and the second is the destination. If josim-cli is updated josim will reflect this since the symbolic link simply makes josim-cli obtainable through another name.

On Windows it is best to simply rename josim-cli or to make a copy thereof with a new name.

docs.text:

The MIT license allows use of this software within proprietary software as long as all copies of the licensed software includes a copy of the MIT license as well as the copyright notice.

docs.title: Embedding JoSIM
docs.text: Link the installed CMake target josim::josim. Use a C++17 compiler and rebuild your application against the headers and libraries from the same installation. The interface exposes C++ standard-library types; a stable binary interface across compiler, standard-library or JoSIM versions is not promised.

docs.title: Parsing and subcircuit binding
docs.text:
After Input::parse_input, call input.netlist.expand_maindesign(input.parameters). This resolves globals, then binds parameters and local models per instance before expanding its children. Do not pre-evaluate all local definitions: some need instance values. Continue with transient identification, matrix creation and simulation as in the CLI entry point. Overrides capture their caller-evaluated values at binding. To change caller/global parameters and rebind a circuit, create fresh Input and Netlist objects; reparsing an already expanded map does not reinstantiate it.

The no-argument expand_subcircuits()/expand_maindesign() entry points remain for existing callers that pre-parse type-scoped parameters/models. They preserve that legacy lookup and component-value overrides; use the parameter-aware overload for named instance parameters. expand_subcircuits() now validates structural dependencies while retaining templates until main-design expansion. Callers inspecting partially expanded templates must adapt to this change.

Resolved instance contexts in expanded lines, ParameterName and models_new begin with |, followed by the inside-to-outside instance path. Definition contexts retain their type names. Local template expressions can remain unevaluated; check Parameter::get_value() before accessing a numeric value. Model lookup prefers the nearest instance before globals. These changes add methods without adding class state; rebuild consumers with this release's headers and libraries.

docs.title: Errors and recovery
docs.text:
Function::parse_function rejects invalid PULSE domains, including a zero period, independently of verbosity. Replacing a pulse replaces its stored amplitudes and timing. Finite cycle counts beyond int64_t use a floating remainder instead of an out-of-range cast. INVALID_PULSE_PARAMETERS is appended to FunctionErrors; existing enum values, signatures and class layouts are retained.

Set finite, positive tstep and tstop before creating a matrix. simsize() checks the point count before integer conversion. validate_output() checks print settings against the actual grid; output also rejects empty result data.

Input, model, matrix, simulation and output failures throw C++ exceptions. Catch std::exception around the complete operation; std::runtime_error::what() contains JoSIM's diagnostic. A failed simulation is not a result. Discard the failed run's Input, Matrix and Simulation objects, then create a fresh run. Solver allocations are released when construction fails or a timestep retry rebuilds the matrix.

CSV/DAT/RAW and model-IV writers explicitly close their streams and check the final state. Standard-output formatting flushes and checks std::cout. A write/close failure throws with its destination; a partially written file may remain and must not be treated as a successful result. WRITE_FAILED is appended to OutputErrors, preserving its existing values and method signatures. If an embedding application redirects std::cout to a failing stream, it owns restoring that destination and clearing the stream's error state before reuse.

Output::write_output also checks every completed trace for finite values. Finite solved unknowns can overflow in unit conversion, filtering or subtraction. Such a result throws NONFINITE_TRACE with its trace label and output-sample index before the normal Output constructor opens any destination. Existing files remain intact. This enum is appended; existing values/layouts/signatures remain. Discard the failed Output object. Applications that populate public traces themselves remain responsible for the data passed directly to formatters.

Model-IV helpers operate on the generated single-junction testbench. Each point rebuilds fresh device state from its bias declaration; timestep retries rebuild from the same Input. Existing signatures/layouts remain. do_simulate honors a positive Input::transSim.prstart() as its averaging start; the default zero retains the legacy latter-half convention for direct callers. At least two averaging samples are required. CLI .IV timing controls are described in the sweep guide. These finite transients do not imply converged DC or continuous state transfer between points.

Transient storage reserves the complete internal sample count only for engaged histories. Allocation/size failures during reservation throw a recoverable STORAGE_ALLOCATION_FAILED diagnostic; the enum is appended without changing existing values or layouts. Output decimation does not shrink internal histories. See memory planning for payload scaling and OS memory limits.

Model::cpr() still returns an owned coefficient copy. cpr_view() adds a read-only reference for callers that keep the Model alive; changes to the Model can change its contents or invalidate element pointers/iterators. Do not mutate the model during simulation. The engine borrows these coefficients and the inductor's existing coupling vector without per-step allocations. Existing copying getters and public layouts remain unchanged.

ProgressBar waits between display updates instead of spinning. Configure its text and total before starting workers; call update while the worker runs, then complete from the owning thread. Repeated completion is safe and destruction joins every worker. Do not concurrently create/complete workers or change their text. The mutex/condition-variable state changes this public type's layout; recompile consumers. Existing stream parameters retain their previous behavior: asynchronous rendering uses std::cout.

Input records the main netlist and included files. Normal output and .iv generation reject destinations that refer to those inputs, including existing hard-link aliases. Keep this provenance when using the normal input parser. Applications that construct expNetlist directly should fill inputFiles if they also need protection for source files they loaded themselves. This adds state to Input; recompile existing embedding applications for this release. Hierarchical pin lookup adds alias state to Netlist/Subcircuit; device differences add a second primitive to RelevantTrace. Recompile consumers of these public C++ types as well. Existing trace-handler function signatures are retained.

Results::sourceCurrents contains only requested applied current-source histories, indexed by the matrix's sourcegen index. Each retained vector has the same length as timeAxis. Unrequested histories remain absent. This appended result state requires consumers of Results/Simulation to recompile.

Results::phaseBefore retains nodal phase at -h and -2h for output conversion. Phase mode retains its solved phases; voltage mode integrates the solved startup voltages with the same BDF2 relation used for subsequent output. The phase origin is zero before the first simulated step, including negative startup steps. Histories are zero when startup is disabled. Explicit selection retains only nodes needing conversion (voltage in phase mode, phase in voltage mode), including difference operands; direct JJ variables need no duplicate nodal history. Default all-unknown results retain every nodal history for later postprocessing. The map stores two doubles per retained node plus map overhead; it does not grow with run length. This changes the size of Results and requires recompilation.

PhaseSource retains two preceding applied phase samples. BDF2 voltage conversion uses these actual samples instead of asking an advanced random generator for past values. Warmup continues through t=0 without resetting history; a cold phase step retains its existing two-sample voltage impulse. Full timestep retries reconstruct the sources and clear all result history. The appended source fields also require consumers of component/Matrix types to recompile against matching headers and libraries.

The command-line helpers CliOptions::parse, display_help, Errors::oor and Errors::error_message retain process-exit behaviour for the executable. Embedding applications should construct Input directly and handle exceptions, rather than calling these CLI entry points.

Matrix exposes its sparse arrays for existing C++ consumers. A simulation rejects empty/inconsistent arrays, invalid indices and non-finite coefficients before calling KLU. Changing public arrays is the caller's responsibility; normal applications should use Matrix::create_matrix.

The legacy Inductor::update_timestep(factor) hook rescales the component's self and mutual voltage-mode stamp coefficients for a finite positive factor. Phase-mode coefficients do not depend on timestep. This edits component stamp storage only; it does not rebuild global CSR arrays or integration histories. Normal simulation retries reconstruct the complete Matrix from Input. Use that path for simulation timestep changes; this hook does not provide variable-step integration.

Model::validate() checks physical/numerical parameter domains. Parsing and junction construction call it, including after area/temperature scaling, so directly constructed models receive the same checks. This adds a nonvirtual method without changing object layout. See the model domains. Updated matrices are checked before refactorization, and every solved unknown must be finite. Invalid models or unrepresentable solutions throw before output; discard the failed run as described above.

Noise::determine_sampling_interval(bandwidth, simulation_step) returns max(simulation_step, 1/(3*bandwidth)), rejecting invalid or unrepresentable intervals. It adds a static method without changing object layout. For legacy direct callers, Input::neB=0 retains the omitted-TSTEP manual-NOISE fallback to the simulation step; .NEB 0 in a netlist is rejected. Automatic thermal sources always require a positive bandwidth.

White Function instances store unit-ASD interpolation samples and apply the current ampValues()[0] on evaluation. Changing that amplitude rescales the current realization immediately, without drawing another sample. Internal miscValues contents are implementation state. Existing signatures/layouts and explicit-interval grid variance remain; the corrected NEB interval changes seeded waveforms. See the noise conventions.

docs.title: Random state and concurrent runs
docs.text:
JoSIM currently has process-global random engines and a per-thread Gaussian cache. It is not reentrant or safe for concurrent simulations in one process. Use one designated thread for JoSIM operations and complete each run before starting another. Use separate processes for parallel circuit sweeps.

Call Rng::start_run(seed) before constructing each run's matrix to select and replay its noise and spread streams. Rng::rewind() resets both streams and the calling thread's cached Gaussian sample; internal timestep retries use it. Drawing from these streams elsewhere changes subsequent samples. Do not interleave runs, reseed another run, or share references returned by noise() or spread() with another thread.

Repeatability means replay with the same build, netlist, seed, timestep and sampling settings. Changing the timestep can change stochastic sample timing. Bit-identical floating-point output across platforms or toolchains is not a supported guarantee.

PNOISE/FNOISE/ICNOISE share one OU-bank initializer. Corrected power-law weights, endpoint limits and sampled-pole gain change their seeded waveforms. This adds a private method without changing class/struct layouts or existing signatures. PNoiseState::scale is now 1 because the variances already include amplitude; S1Hz remains a continuous-OU diagnostic before sampling/interpolation. It is not the actual interpolated PSD or a normalization guarantee at an out-of-band frequency. See the colored-noise conventions.

docs.title: JoSIM audit-resolution ledger
docs.text:
Status: resolved for the supported 3.0.0 scope. See the final qualification. Initial measurements. Baseline: 53b6a426570eafb53d3673f79254157a4ae2c001.

This ledger owns the disposition of the original audit and continues the consolidation qualification. Earlier passing tests do not close the remaining scientific or compatibility questions. Each resolution identifies its implementation, verification and scope. Optional features and documented model boundaries are distinct from repaired defects.

Baseline commands and logs are recorded under build/audit-resolution/baseline/<compiler-configuration>/. Each directory has exact commands/source identity in run.json, compiler/configuration/build/test logs, and CTest JUnit results. The final qualification links the published evidence archive, actual public-download receipts and accepted source identities. Local paths below identify the original repair campaigns; their results remain separate from final integrated acceptance.

docs.title: Final integrated acceptance
docs.text:
• Released source: cb1c42d6fc3cf36f3053f594ba81b7d3290d1164, tag v3.0.0.
  • CI42322270740: all 13 prepublication gates, publication and five actual public-download/native execution jobs pass. Each download passes 63 CLI methods and 200 numerical cases.
  • Four local GCC/Clang Debug/Release suites pass 35/35; full ASan/UBSan/leaks pass 35/35 in 229.02 s. Runtime/test/tool sources are byte-identical across the final documentation correction. Exact release commit also passes local 35/35 and all 13 master gates.
  • Local line/function/branch coverage: 82.431178%/89.230769%/79.378682%; all source/mapping/test-inventory and reviewed risk guards pass. Static review retains exactly 45 assessed locations with zero command errors.
  • The updated release manual is deployed with normal history, externally byte-checked on all 55 pages and browser-checked for math/navigation/examples. The final report refresh and durable receipts are linked from qualification.
  • Earlier per-repair counts and failed attempts below are historical measurements. This acceptance closes their later integrated/native requirements without changing numerical or statistical tolerances. All 11 GitHub issues remain open for maintainer triage.

docs.title: A01 — Same-process Gaussian RNG cache
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed defect; prior repair.
  • Current reproduction/result: Exact replay after odd/even draw counts, same-process independent runs and full-cycle timestep retry is protected. Retry includes white current, phase/flux and automatic thermal noise.
  • Required outcome: Reseed/rewind after odd and even draws; independent runs and retries.
  • Implementation/owner: 64df21c; src/Rng.cpp; test/noise_regression.cpp.
  • Verification: ctest -R regression::noise.
  • Measurements/tolerances/evidence: Draw counts 1–6 reset/replay exactly; retry results/history must match a fresh explicit-final-step run bit-for-bit. regression::noise and regression::library protect replay. Process-global ownership/concurrency limits are explicit in API.md. F07/F11/F16/F17 and their qualification reports record full numerical/build evidence; final integrated qualification is recorded above.

docs.title: A02 — State-dependent JJ thermal amplitude
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed defect; repaired and qualified.
  • Result: F16 reproduces and repairs retained old interpolation amplitudes, missing transition amplitude and sampling before the active slope update. Both transition directions/polarities and six actual circuit cases pass.
  • Owner: JJ::update_value, Function::return_noise, Simulation::handle_jj; test/noise_regression.cpp. Existing slope/thermal constants are retained.
  • Physical disposition: classical local differential-conductance noise, S_I=4kBTG, explicitly not a microscopic nonequilibrium gap-noise model.
  • Evidence: white/thermal study. Six circuit cases give max 5.114e-13 A error against independent SI amplitudes; bound 1 ppm plus 1e-14 A. Full retry must replay bit-for-bit. Broader #107/#108 measurement/example qualification remains separate. All ten native jobs pass for 078f091a1f53 in CI 42268024783, including default/shared libraries.

docs.title: A03 — Modern C compiler incompatibility
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed defect; prior repair.
  • Current reproduction/result: All four final local configurations pass 35/35; C11 and C++17 selected.
  • Required outcome: Explicit compatible C/C++ standards, clean-cache build and compiler warnings.
  • Implementation/owner: 08fd5b6; CMakeLists.txt.
  • Verification: fresh GCC/Clang Debug/Release builds.
  • Measurements/tolerances/evidence: Fresh acquisition and four local GCC16/Clang23 configurations pass; final suites run 35/35. C11/C++17 and native compiler/runtime checks pass in the final qualification.

docs.title: A04 — Installed CMake package
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed defect; prior repair.
  • Current reproduction/result: Default/shared/static GNU16 builds pass 30/30 each, including fresh consumers after moving the installation to a path with spaces. GNU8.3.1 in the pinned CentOS6.10 userspace also passes default/shared 30/30 each. Separate vendor shared-library setup failed from an unset PIC flag and duplicate DLONG symbols; shared JoSIM now explicitly embeds the working static KLU dependencies.
  • Required outcome: Verify dependency discovery, relocation and every supported configuration.
  • Implementation/owner: 30c8fbb; CMakeLists.txt; test_installed_package.cmake; test/consumer; tools/verify_library.py and native library CI matrix.
  • Verification: ctest -R regression::installed_package.
  • Measurements/tolerances/evidence: artifacts/audit-resolution/library-owner and library-legacy contain commands, source/toolchain identities and all test results. The relocated CLI runs and consumers check 1 V plus repeated error recovery; original prefix is absent. ELF loader path is $ORIGIN/../lib. Windows exports/DLL discovery and macOS loader paths require native CI; these are not accepted solely from the local Linux result. CI 42215518336 passes all five binary jobs and four native library jobs. Windows' installed consumers pass, but three build-tree C++ executables cannot locate josim.dll (0xc0000135). Scope DLL discovery to those CTest processes; require the native rerun before accepting this mode. Rerun 42216809204 for 4047755473 passes all ten binary/library-mode jobs.

docs.title: A05 — Silently ineffective SLU=ON
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed supported-behaviour defect.
  • Current reproduction/result: Reproduced acceptance of SLU=ON without an SLU compiler definition. Formally retired: configuration and manual macro requests fail explicitly; supported KLU code is unchanged.
  • Required outcome: Repair and qualify, or retire with explicit configuration rejection.
  • Implementation/owner: CMakeLists.txt; TypeDefines.hpp/LUSolve.hpp rejection guards; dependency_sources.cmake; regression::build_options. Removed unused SuperLU/CBLAS downloads/linkage/exports and compiled-out solver branches. Default class layout is retained; direct users of the removed vendor packages must supply them independently. This retires an inoperative backend rather than claiming untested numerical equivalence between solvers.
  • Verification: Fresh-network GCC Release and Clang Release pass 29/29, including fresh installed consumers and explicit configuration rejection. Manual macro rejection is also covered. Default Release Simulation.cpp preprocessor output is byte-identical before/after retirement.
  • Evidence: build/audit-resolution/backend-retirement-evidence.json, klu-only-tests.xml and fresh-klu/tests.xml; first-party numerical tests retain their existing tolerances. Final platform verification passes; see integrated acceptance above.

docs.title: A06 — Moving dependency URL and stale linkage
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed maintenance/portability defect; repaired and qualified.
  • Current reproduction/result: Fresh GCC Release acquisition/build passed. Filesystem link probes confirm GNU8 needs stdc++fs and GNU16 does not. Both default/shared installed consumers pass with the respective public link requirements. Linux rt linkage is retained for pre-glibc2.17 clock_gettime.
  • Required outcome: Verify immutable acquisition and remove stale links only with compiler/runtime evidence.
  • Implementation/owner: da8998d; cceac6c; cmake/dependency_sources.cmake.
  • Verification: clean-cache configure/build; installed consumers; five-platform ABI checks.
  • Measurements/tolerances/evidence: Immutable archives and hashes are exercised from an empty cache. GNU8/16 filesystem link probes, old-userspace binary execution and relocated consumers pass; final five-platform manifests record their effective toolchains.

docs.title: A07 — Invalid transient and recursive subcircuits
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed defects; prior repairs.
  • Current reproduction/result: Bounded cycle/negative-time checks pass. Additional direct-library non-finite/zero/overflow point counts lacked validation; print starts after the final actual sample produced a generic out-of-range error. Repaired and covered in F06.
  • Required outcome: Clean finite/bounds errors, direct/indirect cycle rejection; no hangs/crashes.
  • Implementation/owner: c36ea8a; 3a11500; src/Transient.cpp; src/Netlist.cpp.
  • Verification: ctest -R regression::cli; sanitizers; malformed-input corpus.
  • Measurements/tolerances/evidence: Bounded direct/indirect recursion and finite/domain/overflow time-grid failures are covered by CLI/library regressions; final full sanitizer suite passes 35/35. See F06 and final qualification.

docs.title: A08a — Named subcircuit parameter overrides (#81)
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed compatibility defect; repaired and native-qualified.
  • Reproduction: both supplied named-parameter circuits failed: RES was undefined without a default, and RES=10 in a header was treated as an IO pin. Preserved six red cases cover both modes and spaced header assignments.
  • Implementation: bind parameters/models before descending into each instance. Evaluate overrides in the caller; resolve local defaults/derived parameters against bound values, enclosing instances and globals. Keep iterative expansion, structural cycle detection, IO/pin aliases, and legacy component-label overrides. Instance contexts are distinct from type defaults. Define exact semantics in syntax.md and the library migration in API.md.
  • Associated repairs: local models now take deterministic precedence over globals; gate shape detection uses the same scoped lookup. Model IV commands resolve type defaults independently of instances. Re-parsing resolved parameters no longer fails; update_parameters resets actual stored values, and redefinitions now perform the replacement their warning promises.
  • Verification: exact #81 circuits return 10/5 V (default-only 10 V) in both modes; independent/nested instances return 31/61 V and legacy overrides return 6/9 V. Declared-name precedence returns 24 V. JJ currents at imposed pi/2 phase are 200/400/100/200 uA for local and inherited models. Scoped positional gate tests give 50/100 uA. Scalar CSV tolerances are 2e-6 relative; gate checks allow 1e-10/2e-10 A (CSV and steady-state rounding). Type-level local model IV samples equal an explicitly identical global reference exactly, while the connected instance retains its different critical current. Malformed/duplicate, unresolved and cyclic expressions fail within bounded tests. Library and fresh installed consumers exercise both legacy and parameter-aware expansion, plus recoverable resolution failures. GCC16/Clang23 Debug and Release pass 30/30; final seven regression groups pass in all four configurations. Full ASan/UBSan/leaks passes 30/30 in 144.95 s; final binding/reparse checks also pass under sanitizers (7/7, 7.18 s). Commit 121ca3ed6439 passes all ten native binary/library jobs in CI 42230226316.
  • Evidence: build/audit-resolution/named-parameters-red.log; named-parameters-four-config.log; named-parameters-tests.xml and final targeted library/gate/installed-consumer logs; named-parameters-sanitizer-tests.xml and named-parameters-final-sanitizer-tests.xml. Quantitative decks, sample hashes and source identity: artifacts/audit-resolution/named-parameters.json. No device/integration equations changed.

docs.title: A08b — Hierarchical pin-alias output (#81)
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed compatibility defect.
  • Current reproduction/result: The exact supplied circuit now resolves V(IN.X1) to the connected node and returns 10 V in both analysis modes. Nested/independent instances and ground aliases are retained. Invalid output requests throw; no successful result silently drops the requested trace.
  • Required outcome: Resolve pin aliases and reject invalid requested traces explicitly.
  • Implementation/owner: src/Netlist.cpp pin maps; RelevantTrace.cpp alias resolution; Output.cpp primitive trace differences. See F05 for accompanying ground-name/output defects, compatibility and measured evidence.
  • Verification: hierarchical output and malformed trace regressions.
  • Measurements/tolerances/evidence: Exact hierarchical pin alias returns 10 V in both modes; malformed requested traces fail explicitly. F05 records scalar/rounding tolerances and additional alias/ground cases; final native gates pass.

docs.title: A09 — Effective seed absent from -V 1
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed observability defect; merged candidate.
  • Current reproduction/result: Found that minimal output suppressed the effective seed despite the verbosity contract. Fixed and tested with an auto-seeded noisy run, extracting its seed and reproducing its CSV exactly.
  • Required outcome: Verify explicit/auto seeds are exposed and usable for replay.
  • Implementation/owner: src/Input.cpp: seed reporting; src/Verbose.cpp.
  • Verification: CLI verbose/seed replay regression.
  • Measurements/tolerances/evidence: regression::cli checks -m 1/-V 1 and --verbose=1, exact uint64 maximum reporting, and rejection of overflow, fractional/negative seeds. Both Release compilers pass 30/30; seven regression groups pass ASan/UBSan/leaks. See F03; same-build replay is an exact comparison, not a cross-platform bit-identity claim. Final native-platform checks pass; see integrated acceptance above.

docs.title: I110 — Original seed support report #110
docs.text:
• Classification: answered support request; distinct from A01.
  • Current reproduction/result: Reporter confirmed v2.7; no issue mutation performed.
  • Required outcome: Document required version and supported option; independently verify reporting/replay.
  • Implementation/owner: https://github.com/JoeyDelp/JoSIM/issues/110.
  • Verification: seed CLI and in-process tests.
  • Measurements/tolerances/evidence: Explicit/auto seeds and effective reporting replay exactly within the same build. Uint64 maximum is accepted and malformed/overflow values rejected; A01/F03 and final native CLI/library suites protect the separate cache repair.

docs.title: I109 — Capacitor initial voltage #109
docs.text:
• Classification: optional arbitrary-state feature; existing silent IC handling is a separate confirmed defect F12.
  • Disposition: No arbitrary capacitor initial-voltage solver semantics are added. Define zero stored histories, finite negative startup and DST explicitly; use a physical charging interval before measurement. A future IC feature must initialize coupled states and histories consistently in both modes/on retries.
  • Alternative/verification: test/comp/capacitor_precharge.cir charges for 20 RC time constants, then discharges after a prescribed finite source fall. Independent closed-form response, KCL/KVL and three-step refinement pass in both modes. Voltage errors are 114.502/29.7314/7.59995 nV; KCL is zero at CSV precision. All four compiler/configurations pass 33/33; affected sanitizer groups pass with leak detection. All ten native jobs pass in CI 42255843921 for descendant 7cbea62036df. F12 rejects unsupported IC syntax.
  • Evidence: support guide and model-boundary study define equations, h^2 bounds, rounding allowance, commands and practical limits.

docs.title: I108a — Finite-cycle sine #108
docs.text:
• Classification: implemented request; analytically and native-qualified.
  • Result: Exact requested SINE(0 315u 4g 20p 0 0 4) stops at 20 ps + 4/(4 GHz) = 1020 ps. Source/resistor current and voltage match the analytic waveform in both modes, including inactive intervals, within 1 nA/1 nV. Direct tests cover delay, damping, phase in degrees, aliases, fractional cycles, defaults, unlimited tones and both sides of cutoffs.
  • Additional repair: F14 makes invalid finite-cycle frequencies fail independently of verbosity and rejects excess arguments; valid sine evaluation is unchanged. This is separate from I108b noise qualification.
  • Verification/evidence: All four compiler/configurations pass 33/33; affected function/CLI ASan/UBSan/leak checks pass in 5.89 s. Sine study, regression::functions/cli, build/audit-resolution/sine/. All ten native jobs pass for 18bb60c9c23b in CI 42259227651, including default/shared libraries.

docs.title: I108b — Switching-dependent noise #108
docs.text:
• Classification: support/model question; state-amplitude defects repaired in F16.
  • Disposition: Classical local-slope FDT amplitude uses R0, transition slope or RN as selected by the active resistive region; no microscopic gap/shot-noise claim. Local temperature overrides global temperature. F16's transition and actual-injection checks pass all ten native jobs. Finite-cycle sine is I108a.
  • External flux/settings: A finite-L mutually coupled loop and separate weak-noise zero-L SQUID reduction now have independent references. The 61-run study quantifies NEB/fJ, timestep, output sampling and physical limits.
  • Evidence: worked guide, study, tools/qualify_squid_noise.py and native numerical fixtures. Final implementing revision passes native qualification; no universal NEB>fP claim.

docs.title: I107 — Floating reference and SQUID noise #107
docs.text:
• Classification: support/model question with validated bounded alternatives.
  • Result: Floating primary voltage source works; removing the island's common-mode reference gives singular-matrix errors in both modes. Twenty-four flux cases cover two h/two modes/two polarities/three reference resistances; independent flux/KCL residual is <=3.713e-9 Phi0, below the 5e-7 budget.
  • Noise result: Sixteen seeds at each NEB=20/200/2000 MHz match an independent weak-noise RSJ reference, with aggregate PSD ratios 1.020164/0.998104/0.992709. Nominal family 99% intervals plus predeclared 5% model allowance accept all. Halving h/print spacing changes PSD by <=0.1413%/0.0612%; both modes agree.
  • Disposition/evidence: worked guide and scientific study explain anchor loading/noise, NEB/interpolation/output and Josephson/plasma frequencies. Strongly overdamped classical example; no general bandwidth or quantum claim. F15/F19 repair bandwidth/output defects encountered. Native checks of the final example revision pass in the accepted release workflow.

docs.title: I101 — JJ-buffer reverse response #101
docs.text:
• Classification: physical response established; separate startup defect F10 repaired.
  • Result: Independent six-state Kirchhoff/RCSJ equations reproduce the active netlist's reverse bipolar response. B02 rotates negatively while B01 returns; reverse net output is -1.38349e-6 Phi0 per pulse. Exchanging ports with the same drive gives 0.999997568 Phi0 forward. The specified input is 4.3 ppm below exact SI Phi0. The original binary/settings are unknown; do not claim exact reconstruction of every screenshot sample.
  • Reference validation: Tightened Radau and separate BDF solutions agree within 2.05e-10 scaled state units (budget 1e-8). Junction voltages remain below the original model's 2.75 mV transition boundary, validating R0 use.
  • Implementation/verification: tools/qualify_buffer.py, independent fixtures under test/reference, regression::buffer; required by binary/library owners. Sixteen full-waveform comparisons cover both modes and four steps. Native CTest uses twelve cases/352 reference points per direction, KCL, loop flux, pulse area and refinement. GCC16/Clang23 Debug/Release pass 33/33; the new group passes ASan/UBSan/leaks in 16.53 s. All ten native binary/library jobs pass for descendant 7cbea62036df in CI 42255843921, covering this study.
  • Measurements/tolerances: At 0.01 ps maximum output errors are 19.1501 nV reverse and 40.5556 nV forward, decreasing about fourfold per halving. Pulse areas allow 5e-6 Phi0; waveform limits scale with h^2 plus CSV rounding. See the buffer study for equations, tolerances, input-variant caveat and source/binary provenance. Full local evidence: artifacts/audit-resolution/buffer-101/report.json and plots.

docs.title: I093 — Stewart–McCumber parameter #93
docs.text:
• Classification: optional model convenience; explicit supported alternative.
  • Disposition: Use ordinary parameter expressions to set R=sqrt(beta_csigma/(IcC)). RTYPE=0 uses RN as its constant shunt. RTYPE=1 has state-dependent conductance; R0/RN choices describe different damping assumptions, so no ambiguous global BETA_C field is added.
  • Verification: test/comp/jj_beta_c.cir derives R for beta=0.2/1/5. Both modes satisfy Icsin(phi)+V/R+CdV/dt, with current errors below 9.40e-13 A against 1e-10 A allowance; KCL residual is zero. All four compiler/configurations pass 33/33; affected sanitizer groups pass with leak detection. All ten native jobs pass for descendant 7cbea62036df in CI 42255843921.
  • Evidence: conversion guide and study; exact SI constants, positive-domain restrictions and zero-C boundary are explicit.

docs.title: I091 — Long-run JJ artifacts #91
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed numerical cause repaired and native-qualified.
  • Result: a controlled raw-precision study reproduces growing voltage-mode phase drift over four lengths, with mode/step/polarity comparisons. An independent 70-digit prediction establishes inconsistent matrix/history constants as the cause, rather than an inference from a single run.
  • Implementation: use the existing SIGMA consistently in JJ::phaseConst_. See F09 for red/green measurements, tolerances and completed local checks.
  • Scope: Constant-voltage and independent current-driven RSJ checks pass native qualification (see F09/D01). The original report has no circuit; do not claim to have reconstructed that undocumented case or explained all artifacts.
  • Evidence: phase accumulation study; regression::junction_numerics. Other #101/thermal/noise studies remain separate.

docs.title: I088 — Nonlinear inductor #88
docs.text:
• Classification: optional substantial solver feature; outside current support.
  • Disposition: JoSIM supports constant Phi=LI. Define whether the requested L(I)=L0(1+a*I^2) means differential inductance or Phi/I: their differential laws differ by a factor of three in the nonlinear term. No per-step L(I) substitution is advertised as a nonlinear solver. Full support requires a flux law/derivative, consistent initial bias/mutual semantics and convergence qualification in both modes.
  • Alternative/limits: A constant-L approximation can be used only within an assessed excursion. For the differential interpretation, abs(a*I^2)<=0.01 bounds departure from L0 to 1% at the element level; this does not bound long-line phase/gain error. Constant-L RL/RLC dynamics already have independent analytic/refinement tests. Large-signal nonlinear/JTWPA behaviour remains outside the supported model. See the derivation.

docs.title: I084 — Parameter sweeps #84
docs.text:
• Classification: scope/support decision.
  • Disposition: .PARAM defines one run; range/Cartesian orchestration remains external. A safe one-marker helper supplies explicit fresh-process points, isolated output, checked inputs/failures and explicit time-weighted windows.
  • Result: R=1/2/3/4/5 ohm at 1 A agrees with IR within 1 nV in both modes. Input/existing-temp/result-directory bytes remain unchanged; actual seed/grid are recorded. Native binary/library qualification requires regression::sweep.
  • Evidence: sweep guide, study, tools/circuit_sweep.py and test/param/sweep_resistance.cir.in. Four local full configurations pass 34/34; final focused/native checks recorded in F20.

docs.title: I082 — IV script and circuit sweeps #82
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed unsafe prototype, plus support/model questions.
  • Result/disposition: F20 reproduces an existing-temp-file overwrite and ignored failures/stale CSV reuse; retire the prototype with a safe explanatory entry point. Distinguish model .IV, fresh circuit points and one-transient history. A tested complete-circuit SQUID sweep is the practical alternative.
  • Measurements: +/-200 uA gives +/-1.13153468 mV against independent +/-1.13137085 mV (0.0145% error, <=1% finite-window/timestep budget), both modes. Zero current gives zero voltage. Source/include/custom data and pre-existing files are preserved; failures and timeouts cannot produce a successful summary.
  • Evidence: guide, study, test/regression_sweep.py, tools/circuit_sweep.py and the retained red witness. Model-IV numerical protocol and broader gate/IV physical review remain explicit separate limits; no adaptive-error/Newton guarantee is asserted.

docs.title: D01 — Numerical regression breadth
docs.text:
• Classification: architecture/testing concern; bounded independent qualification complete.
  • Current result: Independent RC/RL/RLC ramp responses, KCL/KVL and Ohm's law pass for 36 cases: both modes, startup on/off, and 1/0.5/0.25 ps steps. At 0.25 ps maximum voltage error is 13.1534/13.1534/14.0995 nV; current error is 1.31534/1.31534/1.43369 nA. CSV KCL residual is zero; KVL residual is at most 5.00001e-10 V. Maximum error decreases by 3.4–4x per halving, with measured orders 1.75–1.84 (RC/RL), 1.99–2.00 (RLC).
  • Additional nonlinear reference: Twelve current-driven RSJ cases test subcritical equilibrium and above-critical oscillations, both modes and three steps. Period errors are 567.504/142.585/35.6945 ppm and reduce about 4x per halving. Mean pulse area over 820–821 complete rotations agrees with exact SI within 0.092 ppm. See the RSJ study for independent derivation, tolerances and explicit scope. All four compiler/config checks pass; ASan/UBSan/leaks passes all 36 junction cases in 33.58 s. Native qualification passes all ten native jobs for 04ef05788e7a in CI 42235902594.
  • Additional finite-capacitance reference: The #101 buffer study covers two clocked input pulses, both directions/modes, continuous RCSJ references, phase-slip counts, flux area and step refinement. See I101 for measurements and completed native qualification. Six RC precharge/discharge and six explicit beta_c conversion cases now extend the numerical owner; see I109/I093.
  • Required outcome: Complete final integrated qualification and resolve any remaining confirmed numerical defects. These bounded studies do not establish general scientific correctness.
  • Implementation/owner: test/regression_numerics.py; release/library owners require its CTest group. No solver/device equations changed by this study.
  • Verification: GCC16/Clang23 Debug and Release pass the numerical group. ASan/UBSan with leaks also passes all 36 cases (0.60 s). Commit c8a24427ac01 passes all ten native jobs in CI 42231286897.
  • Evidence/tolerances: linear-circuit study derives the independent continuous references, h^2-scaled bounds, refinement requirement and rounding allowances. artifacts/audit-resolution/rlc.json records exact decks, measurements and executable/test hashes. Logs/JUnit: build/audit-resolution/linear-numerics-*.log/.xml.

docs.title: D02 — Coverage and high-risk gaps
docs.text:
• Classification: testing/maintenance concern.
  • Local result: 82.43% lines, 89.23% functions and 79.38% branches under Clang/LLVM23.1.4, up from 57.54%/72.81%/52.47%. All compiled first-party source/header mappings remain included; 35/35 declared tests execute without skips. LLVM zero-hash diagnostics retain exact live execution counts.
  • Required policy: predeclared 75/80/60 overall floors and 80 line/65 branch floors for eleven critical owners, plus review of uncovered decisions. The first expanded 73.77% line result was not accepted by lowering its floor. Later reviewed references guard drops over 0.5 point overall/2 points per critical owner, separately by LLVM major. New majors require report review.
  • Implementation: tools/coverage.py, check_coverage.py, coverage-policy.json; shared CTest inventory validation also gates release/library owners. Eight tool regression methods reject incomplete, stale, skipped and mismatched data.
  • Risk closure: independent PWS/EXP, TX delay/orientations (36), E/G/F/H gains (72), reversed/floating capacitors (12), malformed CSR, control parsing, sanity counts and CSV/DAT/RAW units/data. Piecewise tests exposed/repaired F27. Remaining guard/helper/diagnostic counters have explicit assessed limits.
  • Evidence: coverage study, artifacts/audit-resolution/coverage-policy/ reports/HTML/counters/owners; earlier campaigns remain separate. Local policy passes. CI42307801289 LLVM18 passes all35 tests, mappings and risk floors (81.32/88.95/78.77% in that earlier campaign); its reference is reviewed. The new guard initially used native path separators and failed its positive fixture on Windows; canonical report paths repair that tool defect. The final complete native/guard runs pass, including the Windows archive-name follow-up; see integrated acceptance.

docs.title: D03 — Sanitizers, warnings and static analysis
docs.text:
• Classification: verification concern.
  • Result: full Clang Debug ASan/UBSan/leak detection passes 35/35 for the integrated runtime source in 229.02 s. Solver dependencies are instrumented too; leak checks remain enabled. Earlier failures and per-repair runs are retained separately.
  • Static review: all 49 initial locations have individual dispositions: 44 constructor/topology/immediate-guard invariants, one generated-IV helper precondition, two repaired optional accesses and two removed dead stores. Current ten-owner Clang-Tidy run has zero command errors and 45 reviewed optional-access locations. No new suppression hides those warnings.
  • Evidence: focused review, artifacts/audit-resolution/static-analysis/{initial-dispositions,review-summary,compiler-warnings}.json and current/dispositions.json/raw logs. Existing compiler warning options are recorded, including their unused/sign-compare suppressions. Final clean compiler builds and integrated sanitizer/native checks pass as recorded above. The F27 ten-owner rerun retains exactly the same 45 reviewed locations with zero command errors; final/ holds its current source hashes and diagnostics.

docs.title: D04 — Library recovery and RNG ownership
docs.text:
• Classification: embedding/API concern.
  • Current reproduction/result: Missing .iv model terminated an embedding process (exit 255). Fixed to throw; repeated missing-model, singular and malformed-matrix failures recover and permit a fresh analytic 1 V run. RNG engines remain process-global, with an explicit single designated thread, sequential-run boundary; process parallelism is the supported alternative.
  • Required outcome: Recoverable supported library errors; explicit reentrancy/concurrency boundaries with API/ABI review.
  • Implementation/owner: src/Errors.cpp and Simulation.cpp; docs/API.md. Constructor-local KLU ownership releases symbolic/numeric allocations on failure/retry. Check sparse dimensions/indices/finite coefficients before KLU and check allocation/factorization results. Class layout is unchanged; new diagnostic enum values are appended. CLI termination helpers remain explicitly CLI-only. C++ ABI across versions/toolchains is not promised.
  • Verification: regression::library exercises eight successive failure and valid-run cycles; GCC16/Clang23 Release pass 30/30. The expected DC result is 1 V with 1e-12 absolute tolerance (linear solve rounding allowance).
  • Evidence: build/audit-resolution/library-red.json, library-green-tests.xml and library-gcc-tests.xml. Full ASan/UBSan with leak detection passes 30/30 (131.47 s); library-sanitizer-tests.xml. Final native-platform and RNG retry/replay qualification pass as recorded above.

docs.title: D05 — Maintained Python utilities
docs.text:
• Classification: repaired runtime/data/safety defects; obsolete noise preprocessor formally retired with native alternatives.
  • Reproduction/result: Pandas 3 DAT loading, omitted image dimensions, comparison timelines, phase scaling, input overwrite and phase-spec startup/ reversals failed in actual runtime probes. The noise helper crashed on common netlists and used an incorrect bandwidth clock. See the utility study.
  • Implementation/owner: scripts/plot_common.py, all three plotters and sp_generator.py; noise_insert.py now fails explicitly without file changes. tools/requirements-utilities.txt pins modern NumPy/Pandas/Plotly/Kaleido/ Tabulate. Maintained postprocessing needs no SciPy; scientific qualification tools use their separate pinned environment.

  • Measurements: 14/14 methods pass on Python 3.12.12; five layouts, four phase units, three HTML and eight actual static exports. Numeric scaling/ round-trip allowance 1e-14; independent nonuniform phase counts and timestamps; source hashes preserved. Real JTL HTML/PNG/PDF/SP exports also pass.
  • Evidence: artifacts/audit-resolution/python-utilities/report.json and jtl-exports.json; build/audit-resolution/python-utilities/{probes,tests.log}. Native-platform CI remains a separate final integration requirement.

Native/utility CI 42286617926 passes all ten native jobs and the utility job for 096461bf8b. Subsequent source revisions require their own qualification.

docs.title: D06 — Runtime/memory and trace retention
docs.text:
• Classification: measured-performance concern.
  • Storage result: Simulation reserves only engaged histories from its known sample count. Seven paired repetitions of eight fixtures (112 timed runs) retain identical CSVs and independent analytic/grid/seed checks. Peak RSS medians fall 102.77→89.45 MiB for long noise and 199.77→159.49 MiB for 32 voltages; worst wall median change +0.4%. The initial 15% noise-only heuristic was missed (13% measured); the broader storage benefit and negligible runtime cost justify retention, explicitly recorded without relaxing numeric limits.
  • Contract: raw double payload is 8N(1+retained unknowns+requested applied current histories), before other state/output/allocator memory. Decimation does not reduce retained internal history. Impossible vector sizes fail recoverably without real-memory pressure in the controlled boundary tests.
  • Owner/evidence: Simulation::setup; library/CLI regressions; runtime study and artifacts/audit-resolution/performance/reserve/{summary,decision}.json. All four local configurations pass 34/34; full ASan/UBSan/leaks pass 34/34 in 229.86 s. Native qualification passes in the final accepted release workflow.
  • Copying result: CPR/coupling hot-loop allocation counts drop from 262,144/524,288 to zero in 2,048-step profiles. A separate seven-pair campaign holding reservation constant gives JJ/coupled-bank wall reductions of 15.3%/ 20.9%, noise 7.6%, exact CSVs and at most 1.4% wall/1.2% RSS increases elsewhere. Existing copy getters/layouts remain; Model adds a const-reference CPR accessor. All four local configurations pass 34/34; focused ASan/UBSan/leak groups pass 9/9 in 102.46 s. All ten native and the utility job pass for 9de8d69 (CI42298764991). Evidence: performance/views/ receipts.
  • Progress result (F24): replace polling with a notified 20 ms timed wait. Seven paired default-mode repetitions reduce coupled-RL/RLC CPU medians by 50.5%/50.7%, with slightly lower wall time and identical CSVs. A five-sample run adds no median latency. Eight minimal-mode fixtures also retain identical CSVs; largest median wall increase 1.06%, below the predeclared 5% bound. Independent header compilation and two-worker lifetime failures are repaired; repeated completion/destruction and fresh installed consumers protect them. Recompile ProgressBar users because its synchronization state changes layout. Evidence: performance/progress/. Final integrated/native qualification passes as recorded above; storage scaling and model equations are unchanged.

docs.title: D07 — Source manuals and support claims
docs.text:
• Classification: documentation/maintenance concern, including repaired advertised-help (F29) and installed-manual (F30) defects.

Correct EXP formulas/defaults, ten broken links/anchors and the old plotting snippet. Build dependencies pinned; local context excluded from site/packages.

Real HTML plotting export.

docs.title: D11 — Output and malformed-input failures
docs.text:

docs.title: F01 — CUS waveform path, alignment and malformed data
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed supported-behaviour defects uncovered by D03/D11.
  • Reproduction: all six initial direct regressions failed: no-parent relative path, linear grid, delayed cubic, delayed repetition, fixed sample interval and empty/invalid definitions. The delayed-period case indexed a negative element.
  • Required outcome: sample k at TD+kTS; interpolation passes through samples; final sample holds to NTS, then stops/repeats. Reject invalid inputs cleanly.
  • Implementation: Function::parse_cus / return_cus; Errors CUS diagnostics. Existing enum values and Function object layout are preserved. Correcting the delayed/stretched waveform is an intentional bug fix, documented in syntax.md.
  • Verification: regression::functions plus relative-file/stdin CLI tests; independent linear formula and natural-cubic midpoint 0.6875 for samples 0,1,0. Absolute tolerance 1e-11 bounds floating rounding in direct evaluations; CLI constant-voltage checks allow 1e-9 for CSV formatting.
  • Evidence: build/audit-resolution/cus-red-test.log and cus-green-tests.xml; Full Clang Release suite passes 28/28; focused ASan/UBSan+leak checks pass functions and CLI. Final supported-platform results remain to be recorded.

docs.title: F02 — Numeric literals, expression precedence and malformed input
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed numerical parsing and malformed-input defects.
  • Reproduction: raw 1p became 1, 1e-3/1.E-3 became -2; unary signs in products/exponents, function powers and LOG10 gave wrong values. (2)3 hung in the old RPN reduction; empty/incomplete/mismatched expressions crashed or silently succeeded. The red regressions preserve these individual failures.
  • Required outcome: standard scientific literals, case-consistent SPICE prefixes, mathematical precedence and finite real results; malformed input must terminate with a parsing error. Maintain scoped parameter resolution.
  • Implementation/compatibility: src/Parameters.cpp parse_param keeps the shunting-yard/RPN architecture with explicit operand-state tracking, unary operators and checked stack arity. parse_operator implements advertised LOG10. Misc::modifier normalizes engineering suffixes and rejects malformed scalars. Public signatures, enum values and object layouts are unchanged. Formerly accepted invalid expressions now fail; incorrect valid results are corrected.
  • Verification: independent literal/closed-form/parser-function comparisons, scoped/global operand tests and bounded malformed CLI regressions. Four clean GCC16/Clang23 Debug/Release builds passed 28/28. Full Clang ASan/UBSan with leak detection passed 28/28 in 143.98 s. Direct scalar tolerance is 2e-13 relative with a 1e-300 absolute floor: conservative double/libm rounding allowance, never a solver tolerance. Gross scale/sign errors cannot pass it.
  • Evidence: artifacts/audit-resolution/parser-repairs.json; exact candidate diff hash and run commands under build/audit-resolution/current/*/run.json; units-probe.log, numeric-red-test.log and numeric-sanitizer-tests.xml. All five native supported-platform jobs passed in CI run 42207795568 for ebd832afb83001508dbdc0e92720d56a07fee558.

docs.title: F03 — CLI parsing, input preservation, includes and seed bounds
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed crashes, silent argument errors and destructive output collisions uncovered while resolving D11/A09/D04.
  • Reproduction: --analysis=2, unknown switches, -m 2 and -V 999 returned success; an empty argument crashed. Relative output paths, hard links, .file output and output targeting included files overwrote netlists. Direct and indirect includes crashed. The bounded red suite records 21 failing cases.
  • Implementation: CliOptions retains its pair representation with exact option names and intact values. Reject invalid numeric/flag arguments, unsupported output formats and retired solver/parallel requests. The OpenMP option only linked a runtime; it had no simulation implementation and is retired with an explicit configuration error. Preserve explicit stdin intent. Input records loaded netlists, maintains an exception-safe active include stack, and checks output identity using canonical paths and filesystem equivalence. Output and IV validate before writing. Verbose seed reporting works with minimal output; floating seed expressions must be strictly <2^64.
  • Compatibility: new Input provenance/stack fields require embedding applications to recompile. Existing enum values are retained. Valid CLI long options now honour their values; invalid requests fail instead of continuing. Existing inputs are protected, including hard-link aliases. Unknown output suffixes no longer silently select CSV. KLU/numerical equations are unchanged.
  • Verification: 30/30 GCC16 and Clang23 Release; all seven regression groups pass ASan/UBSan with leak detection (4.71 s). Content comparisons prove every input byte survives rejected output, including model-IV output. Auto-seeded thermal noise replays exactly after extracting -V 1's seed. Max uint64 literal is accepted; 2^64 and invalid seed expressions fail before conversion.
  • Evidence: build/audit-resolution/cli-red-probes.json, cli-red-tests.log, cli-{green,gcc,sanitizer}-tests.xml. Final supported-platform verification and the remaining trace/malformed-input corpus stay open under A08b/D11.

docs.title: F04 — Filename case and logical-line normalization
docs.text:
• Classification: supported input defects exposed by platform qualification.
  • Reproduction: CI 42212510827 passed four targets but failed AArch64's CUS relative-file test after the parser changed wave.dat to WAVE.DAT. Independently, six local cases with mixed-case basenames/directories fail through the same lossy normalization. Blank tab-only lines also crash.
  • Implementation: normalize electrical syntax after joining continuations; preserve CUS paths and .iv output filenames. Retain the legacy lowercase CUS fallback, with resolved-path diagnostics on failure. Ignore whitespace before comments and reject a continuation without a preceding logical line. Existing C++ layouts and diagnostic enum values are retained.
  • Verification: eight CUS basename/directory/spacing/continuation variants must produce 1 V (absolute tolerance 1e-9 for CSV rounding). Model-IV endpoint expectations remain unchanged and now check the requested filename case. Whitespace/comment input must simulate; leading continuations must fail normally. GCC16 and Clang23 Release pass 30/30.
  • Evidence: build/audit-resolution/cus-case-red.log, whitespace-red.log, cli-arm64-failure.txt and cus-case-{gcc-,}tests.xml. All seven regression groups pass ASan/UBSan with leaks (5.08 s); cus-case-sanitizer-tests.xml. CI 42214652354 for fcb4e1f722 passes all five supported targets, including the previously failed AArch64 test. The original failure remains in the evidence.

docs.title: F05 — Pin aliases, ground classification and requested trace contents
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed supported-behaviour defects; resolves A08b independently of the still-open A08a named-parameter issue.
  • Reproduction: #81's pin request was dropped; nested/ground aliases were lost. Unknown/malformed requests often returned success. The red corpus records 13 failures. Names containing GND were treated as ground despite the documented exact-name rule; all six divider/name/mode cases fail before repair. Stricter validation also exposed stale example labels and the advertised C() alias/device differences being ignored or misinterpreted.
  • Implementation: retain/combine per-instance pin maps through the existing bottom-up expansion, bind declared pins before ground classification, and resolve aliases in the trace owner without adding fake physical matrix nodes. Matrix uses exact ground names. Preserve public trace-handler signatures; render documented device differences from two existing primitive conversions. Add current-source terminal voltage/phase lookup and checked operand arity. Fix R2 (absent) to R3 in the output fixture and use the actual nested L6.X1.X1 component in the multiplier example; preserve its circuit equations.
  • Compatibility: unknown or malformed requested traces now fail explicitly. GNDREF/AGND/etc are ordinary nodes. A declared GND port follows its instance connection, including a floating reference. Netlist/Subcircuit/RelevantTrace acquire alias/difference state; embedding consumers must recompile. Existing valid trace column labels and numeric/file formats are retained.
  • Verification: original #81 circuit gives 10 V in both modes; nested and independent aliases give 10/20 V. A floating return gives 15/5 V and a 10 V differential. Divider expectations are 0.5 V/0.05 A. Independent series-network expectations check C(), device/source/mixed differences and KCL (source branch -0.625 A). Fixed phase sources give +/-0.9 rad differences. Absolute tolerance 2e-6 in the trace's units allows CSV rounding, far below the reproduced errors. GCC16/Clang23 Release suites pass 30/30. Full ASan/UBSan with leaks passed 30/30 in 137.19 s; added malformed-selector guards receive a targeted rerun.
  • Evidence: build/audit-resolution/pin-alias-red.log, ground-names-red.log, pin-alias-{gcc-,}tests.xml and pin-alias-sanitizer-tests.xml. CI 42219314943 for df54660779 passes all ten binary/library-mode jobs. Named overrides remain open.

docs.title: F06 — Checked library time grids and empty output windows
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed input/recovery defects extending A07/D04/D11.
  • Reproduction: direct simsize() with zero/non-finite timing did not throw before undefined integer conversion. .tran 1p 5p 4.9p and 1p 1.5p 1p reached an empty output index vector and reported a generic internal bug.
  • Implementation: Transient::simsize owns checked finite/positive/range conversion; Matrix and Simulation use it. validate_output checks the actual final grid point, and Output refuses empty data/index vectors. Direct FIR widths are clamped to the duration before converting tap counts, as in CLI. Public method names/signatures and object layouts are retained; the new output validator is an API addition. Valid grid/numerical equations unchanged.
  • Verification: nine scalar invalid cases plus direct matrix rejection, empty print windows, exact final-sample output (4 ps, tolerance 1e-20 s), and huge finite FIR width preserving a 1 V constant (1e-9 V rounding allowance). GCC16/Clang23 Release pass 30/30; all seven sanitizer/leak regression groups pass in 5.23 s. CI 42221323012 for c5dc995e6c passes all ten native jobs.
  • Evidence: build/audit-resolution/transient-library-red.json, transient-window-red.json, transient-{gcc-,}tests.xml and transient-sanitizer-tests.xml.

docs.title: F07 — Stateful current-source output history
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed numerical output defect; repaired and native-qualified.
  • Reproduction: seeded NOISE current into a single 10 ohm resistor prints source and resistor currents differing by up to 7.406399e-6 A. KCL requires equality. Output re-evaluates the source at past times after its generator has advanced to the end of the run, causing extrapolated values.
  • Required outcome: output the samples actually applied during simulation; capture only requested source histories, include difference operands, retain timestep-retry/RNG behaviour, and test both orientations/modes/filtering.
  • Implementation: capture requested applied current-source samples during handle_cs and consume Results::sourceCurrents in Output. Include both operands of differences; clear histories on retries. Each source is evaluated once per step, independent of orientation/output selection, including both-ground sources. The latter previously skipped evaluation and can therefore change the global noise stream when such a source exists. Results state is appended; existing field offsets remain, but consumers must recompile for its new size.
  • Verification: 16 seeded white/power-law, orientation, mode and FIR/decimation cases have zero KCL residual at CSV resolution. Two non-ground terminal cases check differential-only source requests. Tolerance is 2e-6 relative +1e-20 A for CSV/linear-solve rounding. Requesting source output preserves the same resistor samples; unrequested histories stay absent. A forced full-cycle timestep retry retains exactly one final-run history and replays bit-for-bit against a same-process explicit final-step run. Raw retry KCL tolerance is 1e-12 relative +1e-20 A (double solve rounding).
  • Results: GCC16/Clang23 Release pass 30/30; all seven sanitizer/leak regression groups pass in 5.53 s. Broader PSD/amplitude qualification remains open; this item establishes applied current-sample provenance. Commit 30e311b4a690 passed all ten native jobs in CI 42224588150.
  • Owners: Simulation::handle_cs, Results and Output::write_output.
  • Evidence: build/audit-resolution/output-history-red.json, exact seed/deck and binary hash. Green measurements: artifacts/audit-resolution/current-source-history.json; source-history-{gcc-,}tests.xml and source-history-sanitizer-tests.xml. This is separate from the previously repaired Gaussian cache; the retry test now also protects that fix in a full same-process simulation.

docs.title: F08 — Initial phase-to-voltage output history
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed numerical output/startup defect; repaired locally.
  • Reproduction: an ideal constant 1 V source prints 0 V then 1.5 V in phase mode with startup (1.333333 V without startup), before settling to 1 V. Output fabricated the first two phase-history values. A valid tiny timestep of 1e-30 s also exposed an undefined startup-count conversion before clamping.
  • Implementation: retain actual nodal phases at -h and -2h and use them in output's existing BDF2 conversion. Cold histories are zero. Capture only required voltage nodes with explicit traces, or all nodes for default results supporting later postprocessing. Clear history on retries. Clamp startup counts before integer conversion and reject an unrepresentable interval. No integrator or device equations changed. Appended Results state requires C++ consumers to recompile; API.md describes memory and postprocessing scope.
  • Verification: eight constant-source cases cover warm/cold starts, a single point, FIR output and a 1e-30 s grid; all have zero error at CSV precision against 1 V (2e-6 V allowance for output rounding). Floating PWL terminal voltages match an independent piecewise formula. One/three-cycle phase steps integrate to one/three flux quanta in both modes, within 2e-6 relative, including CSV rounding and the historical constants' precision. The reference uses exact SI h/(2e), independently of JoSIM's constants: https://physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/cuu/Value?flxquhs2e. Repeated library/installed-consumer tests verify deferred trace selection.
  • Results: GCC16/Clang23 Release pass 30/30; full ASan/UBSan with leak detection passes 30/30 in 136.28 s. Commit 100a64307bf1 passed all ten native jobs in CI 42227543389.
  • Owners: Simulation results/history and Output phase differentiation.
  • Evidence: build/audit-resolution/output-history-red.json, startup-overflow-red.json; artifacts/audit-resolution/phase-output-history.json; phase-history-{gcc-,}tests.xml and phase-history-sanitizer-tests.xml. Broader RLC, #91 and #101 studies remain open independently.

docs.title: F09 — Inconsistent JJ phase constants and long-run drift
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed numerical defect, directly relevant to #91.
  • Reproduction: ideal 1mV, rtype=0 JJ loses 1.61822 rad over 1m steps/10ns, and 161.771 rad over 10m steps/100ns, in voltage mode. Raw results avoid CSV rounding. Phase mode lacks this artificial decay. Four independent high-precision recurrence predictions match measured errors within 2.4ppm.
  • Cause/repair: JJ matrix coefficients used HBAR/(2EV), while phase-history RHS used the separately rounded SIGMA. Derive both coefficients from the existing SIGMA; no constant values changed and no phase wrapping introduced.
  • Verification: 24 raw double-result cases cover both modes, both bias polarities, three lengths and two timesteps. Assertions check Josephson's relation, steady constitutive current, KCL and voltage. GCC16/Clang23 Debug and Release pass 32/32. Full ASan/UBSan/leaks passes 32/32 in 175.12 s. Extended 10m-step voltage-mode drift falls from 161.771 to 8.736e-5 rad; phase mode is 8.844e-5 rad. Commit 69b9f1d3b6f passes all ten native jobs in CI 42233555152.
  • Evidence/tolerances: junction phase study derives the cause and rounding allowance, identifies the physical-constant precision separately, and points to preserved red/green measurements.

docs.title: F10 — Junction history during negative startup
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed numerical startup defect; repaired and native-qualified.
  • Reproduction: a zero-voltage, biased JJ/inductor loop settles in warm voltage mode to zero junction phases and IL2=-20uA. An independent KCL/flux equilibrium requires phi1=-0.00245600306rad, phi2=0.003274673rad and IL2=-15.088uA. The old state violates zero applied flux by 0.00759634rad. Cold voltage mode and both phase-mode startup choices agree with the reference.
  • Cause/repair: handle_jj read its solved phase/voltage histories only for i>0. During negative startup and at i=0, voltage mode treated node volts as phase and held voltage history at zero. Read the previous solved values on every step; fresh cold-state vectors are already zero.
  • Verification: eight independent static-loop cases cover both modes, startup choices and two steps. Expected values follow a scalar bisection of KCL plus flux linkage, using exact SI sigma. Phase/current/flux tolerances are 1e-8rad/2e-11A/1e-8rad, including CSV and legacy-constant rounding. Focused noise/gate/raw-junction/numerics groups pass. Independent #101 transient probes now agree between modes and improve with refinement.
  • Evidence: build/audit-resolution/jj-startup-red.log; issue-101/ quiet-flux-red.json, startup-comparison.json, pre-startup-fix.json and probe.log. Original bulky transient CSV attempts were regenerated; compact red evidence and the original source/deck remain. GCC16/Clang23 Debug and Release pass 32/32; full ASan/UBSan/leaks passes 32/32 in 182.98 s. All ten native jobs pass for 4bf3f47e12d1 in CI 42238371973, attempt 2. GitHub's first macOS arm64 library attempt never obtained a runner; retry resolved that capacity failure. Startup study gives the derivation, compatibility scope, values and tolerances. Green measurements: artifacts/audit-resolution/jj-startup.json.

docs.title: F11 — Phase-source and voltage-to-phase startup history
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed supported-output/source defects; repaired and native-qualified.
  • Reproduction: At 0.1 mV constant JJ bias, h=0.01 ps, warm voltage mode prints node phase about 3.03854 rad below the same junction's phase. A warm constant one-radian phase source injects a false 4.93659 mV pulse at t=0 (h=0.1 ps), although the already established phase is constant. Seeded FNOISE phase-source output differs between modes by 0.00332625 rad and resistor current by 1.90786 uA in a controlled cold run.
  • Cause: Output starts voltage-to-phase integration from zero despite negative startup. handle_ps re-evaluates stateful sources at past times after advancing them, and resets derivative history at i=0/1 after warmup.
  • Repair: Retain requested nodal phase history in both modes and actual preceding phase-source samples, preserving cold-step semantics and full-retry replay. No constants/signatures change; appended source state needs consumers to recompile. See the history study.
  • Evidence: build/audit-resolution/phase-source/red.json, constant-red.json and cli-red.log; three new focused CLI tests fail in 21 subcases before repair. The first two records include exact decks and the qualified red binary hash.
  • Verification: Floating/difference traces, FIR/downsampling, single-point and delayed output, warm/cold starts, deferred library output, and raw SIN/PWL/NOISE/PNOISE/FNOISE source samples pass. Raw phase/current bounds are 1e-11 rad/1e-15 A. Same-process full-retry results must match a fresh final-step run exactly. GCC16/Clang23 Debug/Release pass 33/33; full ASan/UBSan/leaks passes 33/33 in 212.16 s. All three controlled red cases now agree between modes at CSV precision. Green measurements and source/binary hashes: artifacts/audit-resolution/phase-source/measurements.json. All ten native jobs pass for descendant 7cbea62036df in CI 42255843921.

docs.title: F12 — Silently ignored capacitor initial-voltage syntax
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed user-input defect; repaired and native-qualified.
  • Reproduction: Adding IC=1m or IC = 1m to an uncharged RC circuit succeeds and produces the same zero voltage as no IC option. It does not apply the requested initial state. Exact red decks/output/binary hash: build/audit-resolution/optional-features/capacitor-ic-red.json.
  • Repair: Capacitor construction rejects a trailing IC assignment with a useful diagnostic and recommends an explicit charging interval. This does not implement IC semantics. A node named IC remains valid.
  • Verification: Six CLI rejection cases (both modes, three spellings), recoverable direct-library error followed by valid runs, and independent precharge/discharge alternatives. Red CLI assertions fail all six before repair. GCC16/Clang23 Debug/Release pass 33/33; affected CLI/numerics/library ASan/UBSan/leak checks pass in 5.19 s. All ten native jobs pass for descendant 7cbea62036df in CI 42255843921.
  • Evidence: optional-features/ic-red.log and candidate.patch; the boundary study defines support and quantitative regression acceptance.

docs.title: F13 — Model domains, transparent CPR and non-finite solver states
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed model/input/numerical defects; repaired and native-qualified.
  • Reproduction: RTYPE=1e30 triggers UBSan floating-to-integer overflow; fractional/unknown RTYPE silently changes behaviour. Invalid D=2 and valid D=1 at finite T/phase pi report success with NaN current. Extreme finite V/R reports success with infinite solved current. Zero-T near-cusp tests also expose cancellation in 1-sin^2. Four initial methods fail in 39 subcases; four further near-cusp subcases fail before the stable expression.
  • Repair: Validate parsed/direct models before casts and after effective scaling. Evaluate tanh(alpha*q)/q using its finite positive-T limit; use an equivalent single-harmonic cosine radicand near the zero-T cusp. Preserve D=1, zero C and signed/zero sinusoidal Ic. Diagnose singular/non-real CPR states. Revalidate updated matrices and require every solved unknown to be finite. No constants/layouts/formats change; Model::validate adds a nonvirtual method.
  • Verification: 120 independent steady phase-bias cases cover four D values, three temperatures and five phases in both modes. Maximum current error is 4.793e-12 A; limit 3 ppm plus 1 pA (largest error/budget 0.0534). Zero-T one-sided currents at pi +/-1e-8 are +/-200 uA for Ic=100 uA. Domain, overflow, direct-model and repeated recovery tests pass. GCC16/Clang23 Debug/Release pass 33/33; final full ASan/UBSan/leaks passes 33/33 in 180.87 s.
  • Evidence: model-validity study derives limits, domains and numeric-cusp handling. Exact red inputs/sanitizer witnesses: build/audit-resolution/model-validation. Green measurements/source hashes and compact compiler/sanitizer receipts: artifacts/audit-resolution/model-validation/. All ten native jobs pass for 7cbea62036df in CI 42255843921, including default/shared libraries.

docs.title: F14 — Verbosity-dependent finite-sine validation
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed waveform-input defect; repaired and native-qualified.
  • Reproduction: Finite-cycle SINE with zero/negative frequency succeeds at -V 0 and fails at -V 1. Its period and stop time are undefined. Excess fields were silently discarded. Red verbosity/exit witnesses and failed tests: build/audit-resolution/sine/red.json and red-tests.log.
  • Repair: Require positive frequency whenever NCYCLES>0, independently of logging; enforce the documented seven-field maximum and update error help. Valid source evaluation/signatures/layouts are unchanged.
  • Verification: Independent analytic waveform and exact #108 circuit assertions in function/CLI groups. GCC16/Clang23 Debug/Release pass 33/33; affected ASan/UBSan/leak checks pass in 5.89 s. All ten native jobs pass for 18bb60c9c23b in CI 42259227651.

docs.title: F15 — Interpolated white-noise effective bandwidth
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed noise-normalization defect uncovered in A02/I107.
  • Reproduction: NEB=64 Hz gives measured time-averaged variance 42.7041 instead of 64 for unit ASD. Linear interpolation requires B=1/(3dt), while the old interval 1/(2NEB) supplies only two-thirds of the requested power.
  • Repair: One interval owner uses max(h,1/(3*NEB)) for omitted-TSTEP manual white noise and automatic resistor/JJ noise. Explicit TSTEP is preserved. Reject invalid/unrepresentable bandwidths; correct stale default documentation.
  • Verification: Eight seeds give variance 63.8564268, 0.2243% below 64; predeclared tolerance 5%, relative SE below 0.6%. Six Welch PSD ratios to analytic sinc^4 lie 0.969538–1.016064, within a justified 30% statistical bound. Four sampling phases/interval ratios check grid versus time variance.
  • Evidence/compatibility: study, test/noise_regression.cpp; artifacts/audit-resolution/white-thermal-noise/. New static API method, no layout change; corrected NEB changes seeded waves. GCC16/Clang23 Debug/Release pass 33/33; full ASan/UBSan/leaks pass 33/33 in 198.80 s. All ten native jobs pass for 078f091a1f53 in CI 42268024783.

docs.title: F16 — Thermal sample scaling, transition state and invalid controls
docs.text:
• Classification: confirmed amplitude/timing and input-abort defects.
