OutputErrors::WRITE_FAILED is appended, retaining both existing enum values. No existing public signature, class layout, file format or numerical equation changes. Successful output retains its existing precision and contents. Failed output can leave a partial file; the process failure prevents it from being reported as a successful result. The repair does not promise atomic file writes.

docs.title: Regression checks
docs.text:
• regression::cli exercises the six actual rejecting-destination cases on Linux, requires nonzero exit and checks the exact destination diagnostic. It also retains missing-directory, malformed-input and input-alias protection.
  • regression::library uses a portable C++ stream buffer that accepts all character writes and fails only at sync(). It requires a recoverable flush exception, restores the original stream, then runs a valid 1 V simulation. Eight same-process cycles protect error recovery.
  • The portable flush regression runs on every platform. The /dev/full subcases are Linux-specific; file-write fault injection on Windows/macOS is not inferred from the portable test. CTest has no skipped tests.

All four local configurations—GCC 16.2.1 and Clang 23.1.4, Debug and Release— compile and pass 34/34 CTest groups. Full Clang Debug AddressSanitizer, UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer and leak detection also pass 34/34 in 211.84 s. The suite retains its independent numerical assertions; this formatting change does not relax them. Native-platform results must be followed for the pushed revision separately.

docs.title: Evidence and reproduction
docs.text:
ctest --test-dir build/dev -R 'regression::(cli|library)$' --output-on-failure

The development guide supplies full-build and sanitizer commands. Local evidence is retained under:

  • build/audit-resolution/output-write/: red/green decks and logs, all-four build/test campaign log, sanitizer build/log/JUnit result.
  • artifacts/audit-resolution/output-write/: compact red/green receipts, per-configuration source/commands/JUnit results, sanitizer JUnit and exact repaired source hashes.

Each local build record identifies parent commit 096461b plus the repair's working-diff hash. The compact source manifest identifies the six implementation and regression files independently of later documentation edits. Final integrated qualification remains required by the audit-resolution objective.

docs.title: Phase-source and output histories — 6 November 2026
docs.text:
Three related supported-behaviour defects were reproduced before changing code:

Case Before repair After repair Warm 0.1 mV JJ bias, 0.01 ps step Node phase loses about 3.03854 rad of startup history Node/JJ phase and both modes agree at CSV precision Warm constant one-radian phase source, 0.1 ps step False 4.93659 mV pulse at t=0 Zero voltage/current from t=0 Seeded FNOISE phase source, cold 0.1 ps step Mode differences up to 0.00332625 rad and 1.90786 uA Both phase and resistor current agree at CSV precision

The first case uses V1 N 0 DC 0.1m, an RTYPE=0 junction with IC=100u, RN=10 and CAP=0.1p, and prints P(N) P(B1). Its first node/JJ phases were 0.00202569/3.040054 rad. Both now print 3.040054 rad. The noise case uses P1 N 0 FNOISE(0.001 1 0 0 1p 100p 16), a 10-ohm resistor and seed 123. Exact decks, red measurements and executable hash remain in build/audit-resolution/phase-source/red.json and constant-red.json.

docs.title: Cause and owning repair
docs.text:
JoSIM uses the BDF2 Josephson relation

\[ v_n=\frac{\sigma}{h}\left(\frac32\phi_n-2\phi_{n-1} +\frac12\phi_{n-2}\right),\qquad \phi_n=\frac{2h}{3\sigma}v_n+\frac43\phi_{n-1}-\frac13\phi_{n-2}. \]

Here h is the simulation step and sigma is the existing Josephson scale. Output::write_output integrated voltage from zero histories even after negative startup. It now starts from the actual retained startup phase. Integration still visits every internal sample before FIR filtering and downsampling; the defect was not decimation.

Simulation::handle_ps evaluated the present source value, then asked the already advanced generator for values at t-h and t-2h. Stateful noise generators cannot reconstruct these past samples. It also replaced negative-time history with zeros at i=0/1. Each phase source now evaluates once per step and retains its preceding two applied values. These histories continue through t=0.

The existing Results::phaseBefore map now supports both modes. During negative startup, phase mode retains solved nodal phases; voltage mode integrates solved nodal voltages. Both begin from the existing zero state before the first step. Explicit trace selection retains only nodes needing output conversion, including difference operands. Default all-unknown results retain all nodes for later library postprocessing. Storage is two doubles per retained node plus map overhead, independent of simulation length. Full retries reconstruct source objects and clear all result history.

Cold startup remains unchanged: a one-radian phase step produces voltage samples (3/2, -1/2)*sigma/h, then zero, with total discrete area sigma. For warm startup that impulse occurs at the beginning of the negative-time settling interval, rather than being injected again at t=0.

No physical constants, signatures or output column formats change. Appended PhaseSource state changes component/Matrix layouts; consumers must recompile against matching headers/libraries. Corrected warmup/noisy phase-source results can differ from old output. The API guide defines the history scope.

docs.title: Regression protection
docs.text:
• CLI checks cover warm/cold startup, one-point output, delayed printing, FIR/downsampling, floating terminals and phase-difference operands.
  • Constant-source assertions use dphi/dt=0 after warmup and independently calculated SI pulse area for cold startup. CSV bounds are 2 ppm plus a 1 pV voltage floor; phase-mode/node comparisons use 3 ppm plus 1 nrad.
  • Raw C++ checks cover SIN, PWL, NOISE, PNOISE and FNOISE in both modes with startup on/off. A standalone generator is sampled only forward in time; prescribed phase and its documented BDF2 voltage/current are checked before output conversion, with 1e-11 rad and 1e-15 A absolute bounds. These test source-sample handling, not the statistical validity of noise models.
  • The same-process timestep-retry test includes FNOISE. All selected raw results and retained histories must exactly match a fresh run at the accepted step and seed. Deferred library output must agree with direct phase-mode results; unrequested converted histories must remain absent.

The three new CLI methods failed in 21 subcases before repair. GCC16/Clang23 Debug and Release now pass 33/33 CTest groups. Full ASan/UBSan with leak detection passes 33/33 in 212.16 s. Compiler warnings remain limited to two unused helpers in the vendored spline header. All ten native binary/library jobs pass for descendant 7cbea62036df in CI 42255843921.

ctest --test-dir build/dev -R 'regression::(cli|noise|library)' \
  --output-on-failure --no-tests=error

Green measurements and executable/source-diff hashes: artifacts/audit-resolution/phase-source/measurements.json. Red tests, candidate patch, full compiler receipts and sanitizer JUnit/logs: build/audit-resolution/phase-source/ and build/audit-resolution/current/. An intermediate build's configure-time version string does not identify its uncommitted patch; final qualification requires a clean exact-source build.

docs.title: Python utility qualification — 6 November 2026
docs.text: This study resolves audit item D05. It covers the maintained plotting and phase-specification utilities, plus explicit retirement of the obsolete noise preprocessor. It does not change C++ simulation equations, the library ABI or the native package format. Usage and migration describe the supported commands.

docs.title: Reproduced failures
docs.text:
Runtime tests used a fresh Python 3.12.12 environment with NumPy 2.4.1, Pandas 3.0.0, Plotly 7.1.0, Kaleido 1.5.0 and Tabulate 0.10.0. The initial audit's syntax parsing did not establish these behaviors.

Owner Observed failure Resolution All three plotters DAT loading raises TypeError because delim_whitespace was removed Use sep=r"\s+"; preserve numeric samples Both single-file plotters Image output without -d raises AttributeError on None.split Numeric dimensions with a 700×500 default plot-compare.py Second trace gets the first file's time vector, even with a different number of samples Use each file's own time column josim-plot2.py Grid/square/stacked label phase jumps but retain radian values Convert phase values in every layout; retain SI voltage/current Plotting CLI -x input.csv exits successfully after replacing the input with HTML Reject input/output identity, including filesystem aliases sp_generator.py No exact 20 ps row leads to zero-timestep division Select the first sample at/after a configurable baseline sp_generator.py A 0 → 1 → 0 → −1 sequence omits the return to zero Track all quantized vector changes; require elapsed quiet time noise_insert.py Blank lines raise IndexError; 10k resistance raises ValueError Retire the redundant parser in favor of native thermal controls

Invalid plotting requests and unsupported image formats now fail with status 2. Modern Kaleido does not export EPS; this formerly advertised format is explicitly retired, with SVG/PDF alternatives. CSV/DAT and whitespace SP file formats remain. SP stability is measured in seconds, matching the old calculation rather than its misleading “picoseconds” help text. Settling-row times and reversal rows change where the old sample-count algorithm was wrong. The legacy rounding threshold remains strict (fraction > threshold).

The noise preprocessor predates native resistor/junction thermal sources. Its flat text parsing cannot correctly evaluate netlist parameters or active junction conductance. Its explicit 1/B update interval also differs from the qualified 1/(3B) effective-bandwidth convention. Maintaining a second circuit parser and thermal model would duplicate the simulator's owners. The retired entry point explains .TEMP/.NEB and per-component overrides, returns 2 and changes no files. Native global temperature includes junctions as well as resistors; the migration guide calls out that distinction and duplicate sources.

docs.title: Regression assertions
docs.text:
test/regression_python_utilities.py passes 14/14 methods. It asserts:

  • Exact trace names and values in five layouts, including trace subsets.
  • All four phase-unit choices in all five layouts; relative allowance 1e-14 covers elementary floating-point scaling only. Other trace units are unchanged.
  • Independent comparison timelines [0,1,2] and [10,20], with unequal lengths.
  • CSV/DAT numeric round trips at 1e-14 relative allowance; unchanged input hashes.
  • Three real HTML CLI exports and eight static exports: three PNGs plus JPEG, JPG, WebP, SVG and PDF. PNG headers assert actual 700×500 and 600×400 dimensions; SVG parses as XML with the requested dimensions; other formats have their expected binary headers/trailers. No image-export mocks are used.
  • Same-path/hardlink input protection, malformed dimensions/options, unsupported EPS and formats, non-finite/empty data and clean nonzero CLI errors.
  • A nonuniform grid with no 20 ps row and expected count sequence [0,1,0,-1] at [21,36,59,90] ps. These values follow the synthetic plateaus and a 10 ps quiet interval, independently of implementation row counts.
  • Two-junction joint stability, zero start/stability, threshold boundaries, invalid phase columns/times/options and source preservation.
  • Both retired preprocessors return 2 and preserve existing input/output files.

The final local suite took about 14 seconds. The receipt records the actual Python and dependency versions, exact script/test hashes, CLI commands and outcomes, exported-file hashes and unchanged source identities.

docs.title: Real output and rendering environment
docs.text:
The current GCC Release CLI ran test/ex_jtl_basic.cir with only its unrelated model-IV output directive removed. Source/effective-deck/binary hashes are recorded. The resulting mixed voltage/current/phase CSV was exported as HTML, PNG and PDF. A phase-only copy produced SP rows [0,0], [1,1], [2,2] at 20, 326.5 and 626.5 ps. The 1200×1000 PNG was visually inspected: separate voltage/current panels, phase panels in 2π units, readable axes and two pulses. This is a postprocessing check; independent numerical model qualification is reported separately.

Local static exports used /opt/brave-bin/brave selected explicitly through BROWSER_PATH, with fresh temporary profiles and Chromium sandbox enabled. The first isolated probe failed because its long task-owned temporary path exceeded Chromium's Unix socket path limit. A shorter task path fixed startup; no browser flags, user profile or host security settings were changed. Interactive browser display was not exercised. HTML and headless export were.

docs.title: Reproduction and evidence
docs.text:
Follow the utility guide. CI's Python utilities job creates a fresh environment, records pip's wheel metadata and installed versions, then requires the same suite with the runner's Chrome. Native CTest remains independent of these optional packages; the tagged-release job requires both native qualification and utility qualification.

Local evidence:

  • build/audit-resolution/python-utilities/probes/: original failures, script identities and synthetic inputs; red.json and additional-red.json.
  • build/audit-resolution/python-utilities/: clean install report/log, installed versions, browser-startup diagnostics and suite log.
  • artifacts/audit-resolution/python-utilities/report.json: final test receipt.
  • The same artifact directory contains jtl-source.json, the effective deck, CSV, HTML/PNG/PDF/SP outputs and jtl-exports.json.

The manifest pins direct packages; transitive versions remain pip-resolved and are recorded rather than claimed as a universal lockfile. Python 3.12.12 on Linux is the measured local environment. The CI job supplies its own exact environment receipt. No GUI, older Python version or other native OS utility runtime is inferred from these checks. C++ five-platform qualification remains a separate requirement for each integrated revision.

docs.title: Assessment
docs.text:
JoSIM has a compact, understandable simulator core that is worth maintaining. The priority is a reliable public baseline: numerical regression coverage, focused noise and input fixes, reproducible dependencies, working library packaging, and accurate documentation. A rewrite or broad feature expansion would increase the work before addressing the confirmed problems.

This was a single-agent investigation requested by Johannes Delport. No simulation code, branches, tags, stashes, issues, PRs or releases were changed. Only ignored setup/context and audit outputs were written.

docs.title: Source and public state
docs.text:
• Public master and v2.7 are both 02a34ee5e7a3a6952b21ccc726fbf7a6d5e2b224, dated 19 December 2025.
  • Public GitHub API read on 6 November 2026: 11 open issues, no open PRs, 112 stars, 41 forks. Last source push was 19 December 2025; repository metadata updates do not imply source activity.
  • Latest release: v2.7. Its five assets totalled 1,671 download events at inspection. These are asset downloads, not unique users or installed-user counts.
  • Last tagged build/release workflow succeeded. Targets: Linux x64/arm64, macOS arm64/x64, Windows x64.
  • Public master is marked protected in the branch API; protection settings themselves were not retrieved.
  • Local noise_research is at the public commit, with no separate committed research history. It contains existing substantive edits and untracked files. Most of the 130 modified tracked paths differ only in line endings; ignoring end-of-line whitespace leaves 13 substantively changed tracked paths.
  • Local work includes PNOISE/FNOISE/ICNOISE, model parsing, phase-step logic, resistor bandwidth changes, Debug code and ignored test_internal experiments. These are separate from released JoSIM and were not rebuilt or qualified.
  • A gate-tunable-JJ stash also exists. It was not applied or modified.

The public commit was exported into build/audit-2026-11-06/public-source for isolated checks. Tests therefore did not exercise uncommitted research code.

docs.title: Branches
docs.text:
Branch Last commit Behind / ahead of master Assessment master 02a34ee, 2025-12-19 0 / 0 Current public baseline, tagged v2.7. gate-tunable-jj a74ae37, 2025-11-26 12 / 4 Only public feature branch with recent independent work. single_precision 90921bc, 2021-02-03 207 / 1 Old float-conversion experiment; unsuitable as a current baseline. testing e0c03a6, 2022-08-17 45 / 0 Fully contained in master; no unmerged commits. gh-pages 8a51dfd, 2025-12-18 Separate generated history Published MkDocs output, not development source. noise_research, local only 02a34ee 0 / 0 committed Existing uncommitted research described above.

The gate branch's substantive delta is eight paths, 110 insertions and 43 deletions after ignoring line endings. It adds gate-controlled critical current, GWIDTH/GC handling and IV changes. The new gtjj_iv.cir is not registered in the CTest suite. Gate indexing silently catches lookup failures; the simulation reads the gate node directly from x_, which needs an explicit voltage/phase-mode review before integration. This is a code-review concern, not a reproduced physical-model failure. No experimental branch was compiled in this audit.

docs.title: Open issue triage
docs.text:
Every open issue body and every available comment was read through the public GitHub API. A title alone is often an inaccurate description of the remaining work.

Issue Classification Evidence and action #110 Seed Resolved support request Reporter used 2.6.10 and confirmed v2.7 worked. Two fresh-process seeded runs matched here. Close after a final triage note; a separate same-process RNG bug is described below. #109 Capacitor initial voltage Feature request No capacitor IC implementation found. Define startup/history semantics before adding it. #108 Sine stop Implemented request plus separate noise problem Finite-cycle sine support is in v2.7 and passed a focused probe. Later discussion concerns switching-dependent JJ thermal noise; that concern remains valid. #107 Floating reference and SQUID noise Support/documentation plus numerical validation Floating-reference explanation was supplied. Follow-up about .NEB, sampling and Josephson frequencies remains unanswered. Needs a validated example, not a blanket bandwidth prescription. #101 JJ buffer Untriaged circuit/model report Includes a netlist but no independent expected trace or comparison. Do not classify the reported reverse response as a solver bug yet. #93 Stewart–McCumber parameter Feature request Useful parameter convenience. Need to define which resistance enters beta_c for nonlinear RCSJ models. #91 Long-run JJ artifacts Numerical investigation priority No reproducer or quantitative tolerance attached. Long phase accumulation, timestep convergence and voltage/phase agreement need measured regressions. Root cause not established. #88 Nonlinear inductor Substantial physics/solver feature Requires correct flux linkage and nonlinear solve/stamping semantics; not simply substituting L(I) into a constant-L stamp. #84 Parameter sweep Previously declined feature Existing answer delegates sweeps to external scripts. Clarify support policy and provide a current example if that remains the intended boundary. #82 ivcurve.py Mixed support/documentation Original script usage was answered; .iv supersedes model-only work. Later circuit-IV and solver/error-control questions should be separated. Script rewrites its input file. #81 Subcircuits Reproduced compatibility limitations Named RES overrides fail; .print V(IN.X1) warns and drops the request. Component-name overrides are not equivalent to named SPICE parameters.

No issue was closed, relabelled or commented on during the audit.

docs.title: Architecture and code condition
docs.text:
The public source contains about 9,500 lines across src/.cpp and include/JoSIM/.hpp, excluding the bundled spline header and external solvers. The major owners are already distinct:

  1. Input, Netlist, Parameters and Model parse controls and flatten subcircuits.
  2. Device classes own matrix stamps; Matrix builds sparse CSR arrays.
  3. Simulation uses second-order Gear/BDF-style history and KLU sparse solves.
  4. Output converts requested quantities and writes CSV, DAT or RAW.
  5. IV owns junction-model IV generation; Python scripts support plotting.

This is a useful basis for targeted maintenance. Device equations are documented next to stamps and in the technical manual. The runtime avoids storing unrequested node traces, and deterministic noise/spread streams already exist.

Important limits:

  • It is a specialized transient simulator with SPICE-like syntax, not a general SPICE implementation. No general OP/DC/AC analysis, .STEP or general initial condition facility was found in the public baseline.
  • The timestep mechanism restarts the whole run at half the previous fixed step. It is not a conventional variable-step solver with RelTol/AbsTol control. The phase-change check starts after the first 1% of the run; this is not a numerical error bound. The cause of #91 remains unproven.
  • Every internal timestep is retained for each selected trace before output decimation. Memory scales approximately as 8Nsteps(Ntraces+1) bytes for double payloads, plus container/output overhead. Long noisy runs matter here.
  • C++ library users assemble low-level objects and can encounter global RNG state. Some error paths call exit(), which is unsuitable for an embeddable recoverable API. No Python binding/package source is present in this checkout, despite historical pyjosim references in issue replies.
  • CTest always uses minimal output and checks process status. It does not assert waveforms, circuit laws, pulse counts, noise spectra, numerical convergence, cross-mode agreement, or installed-library consumption. Several shipped example circuits are not registered as tests.

docs.title: Noise state and amplitude
docs.text:
1. Rng::start_run() reseeds engines, but normal01_noise() keeps a separate thread_local Box–Muller spare sample. Reseeding after an odd draw therefore does not reproduce the first sample. With seed 123, the first draw was 0.79079247321936319; reseeding then returned -0.27958039327489437. Rng::rewind() has the same reset ownership issue. This matters for in-process repeats and timestep retries; fresh-process determinism passed. Owners: public src/Rng.cpp:20 and :88.

  2. Function::ampValues() returns a vector by value. JJ::update_value() assigns into that copy at the subgap and normal transitions. A direct public-library probe changed the junction to 10 mV with R0=160 ohm and RN=16 ohm. Thermal amplitude stayed at 1.2040269706281501e-12 A/sqrt(Hz); the intended normal-state amplitude ratio is sqrt(160/16)=3.1622776601683795, while the measured stored ratio was 1. Owners: include/JoSIM/Function.hpp:42; src/JJ.cpp:238 and :277. This is an implementation bug independently of the remaining physical-model questions about transition-region noise.

docs.title: Build and package compatibility
docs.text:
1. Default GCC 16.2.1 fails while compiling legacy SuperLU's cgstrs.c: cprint_soln() is declared without parameters, then defined with three. Modern default C semantics expose the conflict. Explicit -DCMAKE_C_STANDARD=17 built successfully and passed all 23 CTests. SuperLU is built even when the default KLU backend is used.

  2. Installing the Clang build succeeds. A fresh consumer calling find_package(josim CONFIG REQUIRED) fails because the exported configuration references missing imported targets suitesparse::klu, superlu::superlu and cblas::cblas. The config needs to load its dependencies. A successful CLI package does not establish a usable libjosim development package.

  3. -DSLU=ON configures but does not define the SLU compiler macro. Forcing the macro causes a syntax error because Simulation.hpp also declares a member named SLU. The advertised alternative backend is not selectable through the existing option as written. KLU was the backend exercised here.

  4. CMakeSuiteSparse is fetched from a moving master.zip without a hash; a VERSION label does not pin that URL. SuperLU and CBLAS are commit-pinned. The source minimum is CMake 3.14, C++17; the C dialect is unspecified. Legacy static-build flags and unconditional stdc++fs linkage also deserve cleanup, but were not reproduced as separate portability failures.

docs.title: Input behavior
docs.text:
1. .tran -1p 5p DST on a one-resistor circuit terminates with SIGSEGV rather than a validation error. Transient.cpp:64 checks zero but not finite positive bounds. A self-recursive subcircuit fails to terminate within a 2-second bounded probe; Netlist.cpp:146 has no cycle/progress rejection.

  2. The #81 named parameter example exits 255 with undefined RES. The pin-alias print example exits 0 with a warning and ignores the requested trace.

  3. The manual promises the run seed in -V 1, but Verbose.cpp contains no seed printout, and the fresh-process probes did not print it. Seed selection itself works. This is a remaining documentation/observability mismatch.

Output failure was also checked: requesting missing/output.csv correctly failed with exit 255 and a useful error. It is not a finding against output handling.

docs.title: Documentation and maintenance
docs.text:
• The published homepage and docs/index.md still identify v2.6.5, refer to old Azure build badges and state that the current release is 2.5 elsewhere. Some syntax content is newer, so the manual mixes generations.
  • Build instructions focus on CentOS 7. Current GitHub Actions already provides a better source for the supported platform matrix.
  • Plotting scripts have no dependency manifest. All six Python files passed Python syntax parsing; imports, plotting behavior and modern NumPy/SciPy runtime compatibility were not exercised.
  • ivcurve.py assumes fixed netlist/output positions and rewrites its input file. Document/deprecate it in favour of .iv for supported use cases; do not promise that .iv replaces arbitrary whole-circuit IV sweeps.
  • PROJECT.md was a blank local template; referenced docs/DEVELOPMENT.md and docs/RELEASE_POLICY.md do not exist. PROJECT.md now records discovered commands and ownership. These setup/context files are ignored local material.

docs.title: Verification and evidence
docs.text:
Environment: local Linux, CMake 4.4.5, Ninja, Clang 23.1.4, GCC 16.2.1. Public source unmodified; Release builds; OpenMP off; static JoSIM library; default KLU. Cached dependencies were supplied through FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_CMAKESUITESPARSE, FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_CMAKESUPERLU and FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_CMAKECBLAS. This is not a clean-network dependency-download test.

Check Result Public baseline / Clang default C dialect Build passed; 23/23 CTests passed. Public baseline / GCC default C dialect Failed in SuperLU cgstrs.c. Same GCC build / explicit C17 Build passed; 23/23 CTests passed. Two seeded CLI processes Byte-identical CSV output. Finite-cycle sine Zero output after specified stop in focused linear circuit. 1 kohm / 1 pF RC response, 1 ps step Maximum absolute error after 10 ps approximately 6.18e-7 V against 1-exp(-(t-0.5 ps)/1 ns), including CSV rounding. A sanity check, not broad qualification. Same-process reseed and JJ amplitude transitions Bugs reproduced by direct C++ library probe. Named subcircuit parameters and pin aliases Reported limitations reproduced. Negative timestep and recursive subcircuit SIGSEGV and bounded timeout reproduced; core dumps disabled. Installed CMake consumer Configure failed on missing dependency targets. SLU option / forced macro Option ineffective; forced macro fails syntax check. Python scripts Six syntax checks passed; runtime unverified.

Raw receipts: build/audit-2026-11-06/ contains compiler/configuration logs, results.json, public GitHub API snapshots and comments, probes.py/probes.json, runtime-probe.cpp/runtime-probe.log, consumer failure, dependency tree identities and binary SHA-256 values. The original GCC failure log is retained as gcc/default-build.log. Existing build/ and test_internal/ work was preserved.

No Windows/macOS/ARM runtime, fresh-network build, binary download execution, sanitizer campaign, large-circuit benchmark, full stochastic PSD qualification, or long-run JJ correctness study was performed. Historical CI success and these smoke checks do not establish those properties.

docs.title: Recommended order
docs.text:
1. Preserve and isolate the existing research. Keep master/v2.7 as the public reference; resolve line-ending noise independently of physical changes.
  2. Add a small numerical regression layer: analytic RLC behavior, KCL/KVL, phase/voltage agreement, JJ pulses and long runs, seeded retries, noise variance/PSD, invalid inputs, and installed-library consumption.
  3. Fix the reproduced RNG/JJ noise defects, timestep validation and recursive expansion. Address #91 using a reproducer and convergence evidence.
  4. Pin dependencies, select supported C/C++ standards explicitly, repair the exported CMake package and either repair or clearly retire stale options.
  5. Refresh version/build/example documentation and triage resolved support issues. Retain scientific questions separately from answered usage requests.
  6. Review gate-tunable-JJ and local noise research against that baseline before adding further model or sweep features. No public version change is implied.

All audit acceptance items are complete: current branch/issue inventory, architecture assessment, isolated compatibility checks, concrete reproductions, evidence identities, and recommendations. Repairs remain outside this request.

docs.title: Current-driven RSJ qualification — 6 November 2026
docs.text: This study supplements the constant-voltage phase regression with independent nonlinear equilibrium, rotation-period and voltage-pulse-area references. It uses the capacitance-free RSJ limit: RTYPE=0, C=0, Ic=100u and RN=10. Temperature, spread, gate control and noise are disabled. Here the model's constant shunt resistance is RN; this does not select a resistance convention for the nonlinear RTYPE=1 model.

docs.title: Independent physical expectations
docs.text:
\[ \dot\phi=\frac{R}{\sigma}(I_b-I_c\sin\phi). \]

At Ib=50u the zero-start solution settles to phi=asin(0.5)=pi/6 and zero voltage, without complete rotations. At Ib=200u, integrating this equation over a complete turn gives

\[ T=\frac{\sigma}{R}\int_0^{2\pi}\frac{d\phi}{I_b-I_c\sin\phi} =\frac{2\pi\sigma}{R\sqrt{I_b^2-I_c^2}},\qquad \overline V=R\sqrt{I_b^2-I_c^2}. \]

Using JoSIM's declared legacy SIGMA, the period is 1.19386441898 ps and the mean voltage is 1.73205080757 mV. This continuous reference uses no JoSIM trajectory or discrete recurrence. Separately, the voltage area per 2*pi turn is compared with exact SI h/(2e), independently of Constants::PHI_ZERO.

docs.title: Measurement and results
docs.text:
The 12 cases cover both modes, both bias regimes, and 0.02/0.01/0.005 ps steps over 1 ns with startup disabled. Raw phase crossings after 20 ps define complete rotations; fractional crossing times and voltage integrals use linear endpoint interpolation. Each rotating case measures 820–821 complete periods. Subcritical cases have no complete rotations.

Step Relative period error Error after halving 0.02 ps 567.504 ppm — 0.01 ps 142.585 ppm 0.2513 of previous 0.005 ps 35.6945 ppm 0.2503 of previous

Both modes give these values at the shown precision. Measured period convergence is approximately second order on these grids. Maximum mean pulse-area error is 0.092 ppm against exact SI. Maximum KCL residual is 5.43e-20 A. In the local Clang Release measurement, the subcritical phase differs from pi/6 by less than 2e-14 rad and the final voltage magnitude is below 1.5e-17 V.

The regression allows relative period error 4*(h/T)^2, and each refinement must reduce it below 0.4*previous + 1e-9. The small floor permits accumulated raw-double rounding rather than demanding further reduction below numerical precision. Equilibrium phase/voltage allowances are 1e-9 rad and 1e-12 V; KCL allows 1e-15 A. Averaged pulse area must agree with exact SI within 1 ppm, including endpoint integration and the historical constant's 0.0084 ppm scale difference. This is an average over complete rotations, not a per-pulse shape accuracy claim.

docs.title: Reproduction and limits
docs.text:
ctest --test-dir build/dev -R regression::junction_numerics --output-on-failure --no-tests=error
build/dev/test/josim-junction-regression rsj

The default CTest selection also executes the 24 constant-voltage cases. The constant/rsj arguments select separate tabular measurements. GCC16/Clang23 Debug and Release pass all 36 junction cases. ASan/UBSan with leak detection passes the same cases in 33.58 s. Native-platform qualification passes all ten native binary/library jobs for 04ef05788e7a in CI 42235902594. Machine-readable measurements are under artifacts/audit-resolution/rsj.csv and rsj.json; detailed build/test logs are under build/audit-resolution/. The final qualification will publish compact evidence durably.

The RSJ limit establishes these specific physical relationships. It does not qualify finite-capacitance switching transients, a clocked SFQ circuit, stochastic escape, gap-region transitions or the supplied #101 buffer. Those remain separate requirements. No production equations changed in this test addition.

docs.title: Runtime and storage qualification — 6 November 2026
docs.text: This study addresses D06 through measured changes. Separate stages reserve retained histories, remove profiled per-step vector copies and let progress workers wait between display updates. No simulation equation or operation order changes in these stages.

docs.title: Storage change
docs.text:
Simulation::setup knows the complete positive-time sample count. It now reserves that count for time and each engaged matrix/source-current history. It does not instantiate unrequested histories. Output decimation, trace labels, history contents, retry reconstruction and public class layouts remain.

The memory guide derives the raw payload 8*N*(1+U+S). Vector growth can add transient copies and allocator overhead; unused capacity is not necessarily resident memory. The results below measure actual peak RSS rather than treating a capacity ratio as a RAM reduction.

std::bad_alloc and std::length_error from reservation become a recoverable STORAGE_ALLOCATION_FAILED diagnostic with the requested sample count. The enum value is appended, retaining existing values. A count of 8e18 fits int64 but exceeds any supported vector<double>::max_size(); CLI and repeated C++ recovery tests reject it without attempting an enormous allocation or inducing physical-memory pressure. This check does not promise recovery from an OS OOM kill.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
The clean source baseline is 8e9515ec5c1cac7e5c2d7e3cfbd81f8dfe67e503. The local Linux run uses GCC 16.2.1, C++17, Release -O3 -DNDEBUG, default static JoSIM/KLU libraries and the host's dynamic C++ runtime. Cache, compiler, kernel, available CPU set, binary hash and candidate diff identity are recorded.

Eight fixtures exercise:

  • 64 independent DC nodes with 1/8/32 retained voltages, 600,000 internal samples.
  • The same source network with eight requested applied-current histories.
  • The qualified zero-loop-inductance noisy SQUID: 5.1 million samples at 1 ps, fixed seed 1729, 200 MHz bandwidth and 20 ps output sampling.
  • 128 mutually coupled RL pairs, 128 RLC cells and 128 parallel JJs, each with 100,000 internal samples. Dyadic synthetic timesteps make grid counts exact.

Each binary gets a warmup, followed by seven paired repetitions per fixture, with baseline/candidate order reversed on alternate pairs. All use minimal CLI mode and the same selected CPU. No builds or profiles run concurrently with the final timed campaign. Monotonic time surrounds the child command; captured pipe EOF wakes the supervisor promptly. GNU time independently records wall, user/system CPU and peak RSS. The archive retains medians, quartiles and ranges.

A provisional wrapper used timeout polling with file-directed stdout, which quantized its supervisor wall time by up to 50 ms. Those wall results are excluded. The final campaign was repeated with the corrected method; its owner hashes distinguish it from the preserved provisional evidence.

The owner validates finite, strictly increasing samples, exact grids/seeds, analytic DC voltages/source currents, RL/RLC equilibria and symmetric-JJ KCL. The noisy mean has a 3 nV allowance around the independently derived weak-noise RSJ mean; the longer scientific study establishes its model/statistical scope. Every paired CSV hash must match exactly. All 112 timed runs pass these unchanged assertions and all paired outputs are byte-identical.

docs.title: Reservation results
docs.text:
Median wall time and peak resident memory:

Workload Baseline seconds Reserved seconds Baseline MiB Reserved MiB 128 JJs 0.3098 0.3110 10.13 10.05 128 coupled RL pairs 0.6166 0.6166 11.66 10.71 128 RLC cells 0.3868 0.3866 9.94 9.70 Eight applied-source histories 0.4318 0.4141 59.63 47.66 Long noisy SQUID 0.5219 0.5115 102.77 89.45 One voltage history 0.4055 0.4002 18.97 15.15 32 voltage histories 0.4780 0.4453 199.77 159.49 Eight voltage histories 0.4220 0.4132 56.80 47.68

Peak memory falls about 13% for the noisy run and 20% for 32 voltages or eight applied-current histories. The widest case's wall median falls 6.8%; the worst median wall change is +0.4%. Baseline allocator-dependent RSS varies across repetitions, particularly the eight-history cases; full quartiles are retained rather than presenting one favorable run.

The initial engineering heuristic sought a 15% noisy-run RSS reduction. That single-workload heuristic was not met. The change is retained for the measured broader 20% storage benefit, 13% noisy-run benefit and negligible runtime cost. The decision receipt states the missed heuristic explicitly; no numerical assertion or performance-regression limit was relaxed. This is a bounded engineering result, not a universal speed or memory guarantee.

docs.title: Per-step vector copies
docs.text:
Callgrind 3.25.1 identified two allocation sites in otherwise read-only loops. For 2,048 steps, a 128-JJ profile performed 262,144 allocations/frees inside handle_jj; a 256-inductor profile performed 524,288 inside handle_inductors. These counts equal one vector copy per device per step. Parser/setup allocations are separate. Removing these copies makes both hot-function allocation counts zero; the profiled CSV outputs remain byte-identical.

The engine borrows CPR coefficients through Model::cpr_view() and reads the inductor's existing public coupling vector directly. Existing copying getters retain their signatures and behavior. The new CPR accessor returns a const reference tied to its live Model; no class layout or numerical formula changes. The engine does not mutate either collection while using it.

A separate seven-pair campaign holds reservation constant on both sides, using clean source ca3c516 as its baseline. It repeats the same eight fixtures and assertions with the corrected clock. All 112 timed runs pass and all paired CSVs match exactly:

Workload Before seconds Borrowed-read seconds Wall reduction 128 JJs 0.3089 0.2616 15.3% 128 coupled RL pairs 0.6164 0.4877 20.9% Long noisy SQUID 0.5174 0.4780 7.6%

JJ/coupled-bank CPU medians fall about 17%/21%. The largest wall increase among the other fixtures is 1.4%, within the predeclared 5% regression limit. Peak RSS stays within 1.2% on every case. Both target banks exceed the predeclared 5% improvement requirement. These are separate measurements, not sums of percentage gains from different stages.

artifacts/audit-resolution/performance/views/ retains the exact comparison owners, all per-run receipts, source/binary identities, profiles and annotated call trees. Its baseline already includes reservation, so these gains isolate the two copying sites through the pure-JJ and pure-inductor fixtures.

docs.title: Progress workers
docs.text:
The clean baseline is 9de8d69a8ff4925ecd0256b5a1e50ecca63e5f7d, which already includes both earlier stages. The old progress worker continually polled atomic values. It now waits up to 20 ms between updates; completion notifies it immediately, so finishing a short run does not require that delay. Internal callers configure text and total before starting the worker.

Two public-helper defects were reproduced separately: including its header alone failed to compile because of missing includes, and creating two workers then destroying the bar aborted because only the last thread was joined. The header is now self-contained; completion/destruction joins all workers and repeated completion is safe. Installed-consumer and repeated embedding tests protect these contracts. Added synchronization state changes ProgressBar's layout; consumers must recompile. This does not add simulation parallelism.

A separate seven-pair campaign uses two available CPUs, default progress mode, the same CSV/numerical checks and the corrected clock above. All 42 timed runs pass with identical paired CSVs:

Workload Before wall seconds Waiting wall seconds Before CPU seconds Waiting CPU seconds 128 coupled RL pairs 0.5041 0.4939 0.97 0.48 128 RLC cells 0.3923 0.3853 0.75 0.37 Five-sample DC run 0.002405 0.002070 below timer resolution below timer resolution

Both medium cases exceed the predeclared 40% CPU-reduction requirement and have no wall regression. The small-run median adds no latency, within its predeclared 5 ms absolute allowance; its millisecond result is not a general speed claim. Peak RSS changes by at most +0.33% in the medium cases.

Minimal mode creates no progress worker but still constructs the helper. Another seven-pair campaign repeats all eight earlier fixtures in minimal mode: all 112 timed runs pass, every paired CSV is identical, and the largest median wall increase is 1.06%, within the predeclared 5% regression limit. Peak RSS changes by at most +0.59%. No numerical tolerance was changed. artifacts/audit-resolution/performance/progress/ retains both summaries, per-run receipts, exact owners, fixtures, source/binary hashes and the independent header/lifetime red/green evidence.

docs.title: Verification and evidence
docs.text:
All four local GCC/Clang Debug/Release configurations pass 34/34 CTest groups, including new CLI and repeated embedding storage-limit checks. Full Clang Debug ASan/UBSan and leak detection pass 34/34 in 229.86 s. Native-platform qualification remains required for the pushed revision; it is not inferred from the benchmark's Release runs.

The vector-copy stage also passes all four local 34/34 suites. Its focused ASan/UBSan/leak campaign passes 9/9 groups in 102.46 s, covering junction, coupling, noise, installed-consumer and recovery paths. Final integrated full sanitizer/native qualification remains required separately.

The progress stage passes all four local 34/34 suites and full Clang Debug ASan/UBSan/leak detection, 34/34 in 211.29 s. Its fresh installed consumer includes the progress header first and completes a worker twice. Repeated library runs also destroy two-worker bars with and without explicit completion. The preceding vector-copy source passes all ten native binary/library jobs and the utility job in CI42298764991. Each subsequent pushed revision still requires its own native checks.

artifacts/audit-resolution/performance/reserve/ contains summary.json, the explicit decision.json, all per-repetition receipts, fixtures and exact measure.py/paired_reserve.py owners. Detailed timing logs and CSV witnesses remain under build/audit-resolution/performance/paired-reserve-final/. Baseline/candidate binary and source identities are retained separately.

To reproduce the archived owner, run from a source checkout. Place the two corresponding Release executables at build/audit-resolution/performance/bin/{baseline,reserve-candidate}, copy its eight fixtures into build/audit-resolution/performance/fixtures/, and place the owners in that performance directory. Run:

python -B build/audit-resolution/performance/paired_reserve.py

The result directory must be new; prior results are preserved. This task-owned Linux measurement owner uses GNU time and taskset. It is not part of portable CTest or a claim about runtime on other operating systems.

docs.title: Finite sine cycles (#108) — 6 November 2026
docs.text:
The original requested source SINE(0 315u 4g 20p 0 0 4) is implemented. Its stop time is

\[ t_{end}=T_D+N_C/f=20\text{ ps}+4/(4\text{ GHz})=1020\text{ ps}. \]

A 1-ohm load provides independent current/voltage checks in both analysis modes, at 5 ps steps through 1100 ps. Applied source current, resistor current and voltage must match the analytic sine within 1 nA/1 nV, including zero before the delay and after the fourth cycle. The assertions require samples in the active peaks and after the stop, rather than merely a successful run.

Direct waveform tests cover SIN/SINE aliases, nonzero offset, 30-degree phase, damping, delayed start, default frequency, fractional cycles and zero/negative cycle counts. The expected equation is calculated independently using standard sin/exp, including both sides of the cutoff. A positive cycle count specifies duration N_C/f after the delay; phase does not change that duration. Nonpositive or omitted N_C selects an unlimited tone. Stopping returns to the DC offset, which can be discontinuous when the tone has a nonzero phase at its cutoff.

Validation exposed a separate defect: finite cycles with zero/negative frequency were accepted at verbosity 0 and rejected at verbosity 1. They are now rejected consistently. More than seven arguments also fails explicitly. Error help now shows the phase and cycle-count fields. Valid waveform evaluation is unchanged.

GCC16/Clang23 Debug and Release pass all 33 CTest groups. Affected function/CLI ASan/UBSan checks with leak detection pass in 5.89 s; the preceding production revision passed the complete 33-group suite in 180.87 s. Commit 18bb60c9c23b023f9ec5b6a9bc98a447e9253bdf passes all ten native binary and default/shared-library jobs in CI 42259227651.

ctest --test-dir build/dev -R 'regression::(functions|cli)' \
  --output-on-failure --no-tests=error

Owners: test/function_regression.cpp and test/regression_cli.py. Red decks, verbosity-dependent exit codes, failed tests, source patch and green receipts are under build/audit-resolution/sine/. This closes the original finite-cycle request; switching-dependent noise and external-flux discussions in the same issue retain their separate qualification work.

docs.title: Floating references, flux and SQUID noise — 6 November 2026
docs.text: Two bounded examples address the support questions in #107/#108. The finite-L example checks electrical references and external mutual flux. A separate zero-L reduction provides an independently checkable classical noise response. Neither implements quantum dynamics, nonequilibrium quasiparticle noise or a general magnetic-field solver. The user guide gives commands.

docs.title: Floating primary and finite-L equilibrium
docs.text:
The primary has L=100 pH and a 1-ohm series resistor. Its voltage source is between two non-ground nodes. Mutuals to the two 5 pH SQUID arms are -5/+5 pH. Their squared coupling coefficients sum to 0.1, below 1, so the three-inductor energy matrix is positive definite. With no transport bias, KCL gives opposite arm currents. Flux linkage and the sinusoidal current-phase relation give

\[ 2\sigma\arcsin(I/I_c)+(L_1+L_2)I=(M_2-M_1)I_P,\qquad \sigma=\frac{h_{Planck}}{4\pi e}. \]

For \(I_c=1\) mA and applied flux \(0.25\Phi_0\), independent scalar bisection gives \(I_P=51.6958462115\) uA, circulating current 48.5021253127 uA and junction phases \(\pm0.0485211619925\) rad. The 24 native cases cover two modes, 1/0.5 ps steps, both flux polarities and 1-ohm/1-megohm/1-gigaohm reference resistors. After 10 ns, assertions require current error <=20 pA, phase error <=1e-8 rad, flux residual <5e-7 Phi0 and reference current/KCL residual <1 fA. The budgets include CSV and retained physical-constant rounding. Measured maximum flux residual is 3.713e-9 Phi0. Removing the reference gives a useful singular-matrix error in both modes, after removing the now-invalid reference current trace request too.

The anchor fixes the island's common-mode voltage and carries no loop current in this circuit. It has TEMP=0 so a global thermal setting cannot turn the numerical anchor into an unintended noise source. Other circuits can have physical common-mode paths; the anchor's insignificance must be checked there. This establishes a floating voltage source and applied loop flux, independently of claims about a complete SQUID amplifier or its parasitics.

docs.title: Independent weak-noise reference
docs.text:
For equal junctions with negligible loop inductance and external flux f in flux quanta, the two sinusoidal currents reduce to one effective RSJ:

\[ I_c^{eff}=2I_c\cos(\pi f),\quad R_{eff}=R_N/2,\quad C_{eff}=2C, \qquad \dot\psi=\frac{R_{eff}}{\sigma}(I_b-I_c^{eff}\sin\psi+\delta I). \]

The circuit retains finite C; the reference neglects its effect in the strongly overdamped, weak-noise limit. At f=0.25, each Ic=1 mA/RN=1 milliohm/C=10 pF, and Ib=1.6 mA, the independent SI values are:

Quantity Value Effective Ic / R / C 1.41421356 mA / 0.5 milliohm / 20 pF Mean voltage, R sqrt(Ib²-Ic_eff²) 0.374165739 uV Josephson frequency, mean voltage/Phi0 180.945746 MHz Effective plasma frequency 73.772542 GHz beta_c / Gamma=kBT/(Ic_eff sigma) 2.14857e-5 / 1.24590e-4 Classical scale kBT/h at 4.2 K 87.513800 GHz

Let \(D=I_b^2-(I_c^{eff})^2\). Transform the noiseless running phase to a uniform angle theta. Its small-noise phase-response factor is \(Z(\theta)=(I_b+I_c^{eff}\cos\theta)/\sqrt D\). The constant and first harmonic mix current noise into low-frequency voltage noise, giving

\[ S_V(f)\simeq\frac{R_{eff}^2}{D}\left[ I_b^2S_I(f)+\frac{(I_c^{eff})^2}{4} \{S_I(f_J+f)+S_I(f_J-f)\}\right]. \]

The two independent shunts supply \(S_I(f)=4k_BT/R_{eff}\;\operatorname{sinc}^4(f/(3NEB))\). This reference uses exact SI constants and the independently derived interpolation transfer, not JoSIM output or fitted amplitudes. In the broad-white limit at f≈0 it reduces to \(4k_BTR_{eff}[I_b^2+(I_c^{eff})^2/2]/D\); for noise far narrower than fJ, the mixing term is suppressed. This is why bandwidth can affect measured low-frequency noise even in an overdamped circuit.

docs.title: Protocol and measured acceptance
docs.text:
tools/qualify_squid_noise.py owns the fixed scientific campaign; optional dependencies are pinned in tools/requirements-qualification.txt. Sixteen seeds at each of three bandwidths, plus four noiseless mode/step cases and nine paired refinements, give 61 runs. Each discards 100 ns and measures 5 us. The base internal step is 2 ps, output spacing 20 ps, with no FIR. Verbose output verifies the final internal step and computed count, so a full-run retry cannot silently change the experiment.

Welch analysis uses 0.5 us periodic-Hann windows, 50% overlap and separate 4/8/12/16/20 MHz bins. Each seed's primary statistic is the mean of its five PSD/reference ratios. The between-seed standard error gives a Student-t interval, using a Bonferroni correction for nominal 99% family confidence over three bands (critical t=3.483677, 15 degrees of freedom). A predeclared 5% systematic allowance covers weak-noise/finite-C/low-frequency and window approximations; acceptance is |ensemble mean ratio-1| <= statistical half-width +0.05. This is an aggregate-band criterion; individual bins retain sampling scatter. No amplitude is fitted to the simulator.

NEB NEB/fJ Mean PSD/reference Statistical half-width 20 MHz 0.110530 1.020164 0.067364 200 MHz 1.105304 0.998104 0.123052 2 GHz 11.053037 0.992709 0.064432

All pass the declared criterion. Actual mean measured voltage PSDs across the five bins are 0.401566/0.638990/0.730640 pV²/Hz, compared with independent 0.393702/0.640216/0.736007. At the lowest bandwidth, the measurement band also approaches the noise rolloff; the reference explicitly includes that attenuation. The higher-band changes include noise mixed down from near fJ. Every tested bandwidth remains far below the bare plasma frequency; this particular strongly overdamped model does not require driving noise through that resonance.

Paired seed-101 checks hold the physical noise interval fixed. Halving h to 1 ps changes any primary-bin PSD by at most 0.1413%. Halving output spacing to 10 ps changes it by at most 0.0612%. Switching analysis mode changes it by at most 9.059e-7 relative. Each is below the predeclared 1% refinement bound. Noiseless periods err by 1.9803 ppm at 2 ps and 0.5138 ppm at 1 ps in both modes, improving about fourfold. Mean-voltage error is below 0.164 nV, inside the 1 nV finite-record allowance. Noiseless period allowance is 10 ppm.

The sampled PSD equation assumes weak classical fluctuations, fixed bias, negligible screening and low measurement frequencies relative to fJ. It does not justify a universal NEB>fJ or NEB>fP prescription. Underdamped resonances, larger noise, switching, finite loop inductance or other noise mechanisms need their own physical model and bandwidth/timestep convergence checks.

docs.title: Defects uncovered by the example
docs.text:
F18 rejects excess NOISE/PNOISE/FNOISE/ICNOISE arguments, previously discarded silently in four reproduced cases. Direct-library and clean-CLI tests protect the documented syntax. Verbose output also now reports effective timestep and computed count; a 2 ps requested grid reduced to 0.25 ps reports 512 actual points over 128 ps in both modes.

F19 repairs output selection. A 1 ps internal grid with 10 ps print spacing previously emitted 9/10/11 ps gaps because cumulative target addition crossed floating grid ties inconsistently. Select targets directly with fma and a few-ulp tie allowance; do not interpolate output. Both modes and integer/ fractional starts check all 1990 timestamps against independent integer-index expectations. General nonintegral step ratios still select actual nonuniform internal samples. Device equations, physical constants and file columns are unchanged; corrected output sample choices intentionally change affected files.

Source/fixture/binary hashes, exact decks, logs, per-seed PSDs, uncertainty and figures are under artifacts/audit-resolution/squid-noise/. The exact final 61-run owner is preserved there as qualification-owner.py, matching the current tool's recorded hash. It verifies reported seeds and effective steps, and checks source/binary stability. Both PNG and PDF were generated; the plot was inspected. Raw reproducible transient CSVs were removed after analysis; their hashes and complete generation inputs remain. Peak child RSS was 145.7 MiB; concurrent build/sanitizer activity means these timings are not a controlled performance benchmark. Native numerical receipts and red print-grid witnesses are under build/audit-resolution/squid-example/.

The candidate is based on cb594a3 plus the F18/F19/example changes. All four GCC16/Clang23 Debug/Release configurations pass 33/33; the full ASan/UBSan suite with leak detection passes 33/33 in 209.52 s. A subsequent explicit standard-header include was compiled in all four CLI builds; numerical behavior was unchanged. Native results for the implementing revision remain pending in the audit ledger. Final integration/release/site qualification remains separate.

docs.title: Safe external sweeps — 6 November 2026
docs.text: This resolves the unsafe ivcurve.py prototype and supplies bounded alternatives for #82/#84. It does not introduce an internal multidimensional sweep engine. The guide distinguishes model, fresh-point and continuous-history measurements and gives executable commands.

docs.title: Reproduced failure and disposition
docs.text:
The original script assumes the current is token 9 on physical line 2. It derives output/temp names through case-sensitive .cir replacement, edits files directly, ignores subprocess status and reads fixed CSV columns. Its phase-derived voltage calculation also has incorrect dimensions.

A bounded probe used task-owned inputs and an existing input_tmp.cir sentinel. The simulator wrapper ran real JoSIM once, then returned status 17. Within five seconds the script made 292 calls, overwrote the sentinel and repeatedly reused the first CSV despite subsequent failures. The original main netlist was unchanged in this particular probe. The defect is the demonstrated unrelated temporary-file overwrite and unchecked/stale execution, not a claim that every input filename is overwritten. Exact old script/binary hashes and witnesses are in build/audit-resolution/sweeps/unsafe-iv/red.json and red.log.

The prototype is formally retired. Its old entry point now returns status 2 with useful alternatives and changes no files. Git preserves its history. This avoids retaining a misleading special-purpose script as a supported general circuit-IV workflow.

docs.title: Replacement ownership and numerical checks
docs.text:
tools/circuit_sweep.py replaces a finite numeric @VALUE@ marker in a main template and launches one fresh CLI process per value. Standard input plus the template working directory preserves relative source paths. Preflight checks all reachable include contexts, rejects FILE/IV output directives, and hashes netlists/includes/custom data. Generated output uses a new directory and a unique absolute CLI output path per point. No original netlist is edited. Every result records effective seed/grid and source/binary/output identity.

The explicit-window average is

\[ \bar y=\frac{1}{t_b-t_a}\sum_k \frac{y_k+y_{k+1}}2(t_{k+1}-t_k), \]

using the piecewise-linear trace clipped/interpolated to the two boundaries. No extrapolation is permitted. A deliberately nonuniform grid for y=2t has exact mean 3.5 over [0.5,3], which independently checks boundary clipping and weighting. Invalid/nonfinite/duplicate timestamps fail cleanly.

Native regression assertions include:

  • Five R=1/2/3/4/5-ohm points driven by 1 A: each mean agrees with IR within 1 nV in both analysis modes. Controlled seed 123 and 20 computed points are recorded, and source/existing-temp-file/result-directory byte preservation is required.
  • A complete two-junction zero-L circuit at -200/0/+200 uA: independent overdamped mean voltages are -1.13137085/0/+1.13137085 mV. Measured values are -1.13153468/0/+1.13153468 mV in both modes, 0.0145% relative error. The 1% bound includes endpoint phase uncertainty <=Phi0/(490 ps)=4.23 uV and timestep/CSV error at about 183 points per Josephson period.
  • Relative nested inputs and a continued mixed-case CUS waveform: resistor currents agree with 1/R within 1 nA, external-data hashes are recorded, and all input bytes remain unchanged. Filenames/working paths contain spaces.
  • Nested FILE/IV rejection happens before execution/output creation. Invalid values/windows/timeouts and recursive includes fail usefully. A simulator error stops at its first point with no summary CSV or stale-data reuse.
  • A bounded timeout preserves the effective input and partial log as a failure. The retired prototype cannot modify either a source or an existing temp file.

The helper supports one numeric marker in the main template, fixed include/data filenames and within-file continuations. It does not silently transform model IV directives, interpolate solver states, promise stationary noise from one record, or carry state between independent points. General multidimensional sweeps remain external orchestration, with explicitly chosen combinations and state/seed policies.

docs.title: Qualification
docs.text:
The new standard-library regression::sweep group is required by binary and installed-library qualification. All four local compiler/configurations pass 34/34 CTest groups. The final expanded nine-test sweep group passes all four configurations and ASan/UBSan with leak detection in 4.02 s. The preceding production revision passed the complete 33-group sanitizer suite in 209.52 s; this batch changes Python workflows/test registration, with no C++ equation or runtime change. Broader Plotly/Pandas utility/dependency work remains separate under D05.

Reproduce from the repository root:

ctest --test-dir build/dev -R regression::sweep --output-on-failure --no-tests=error

Detailed source hashes, exact red witnesses, analytic measurements and compiler/ sanitizer receipts are under build/audit-resolution/sweeps/ and compact artifacts/audit-resolution/sweeps/. Native final-revision qualification remains pending; no version/release/site completion is implied.

docs.title: White bandwidth and junction thermal noise — 6 November 2026
docs.text: This study repairs F15/F16 and completes the state-amplitude part of A02. It does not close the broader SQUID/noise example or colored-noise work.

docs.title: Effective bandwidth
docs.text:
Let independent Gaussian update values have variance \(\sigma_y^2=A^2/(2\Delta)\), where \(A\) is the one-sided ASD and \(\Delta\) is the update interval. Linear interpolation at fractional position \(u\) has variance \(\sigma_y^2[(1-u)^2+u^2]\). Averaging over one interval gives

\[ \overline{\sigma_x^2}=\frac23\sigma_y^2=\frac{A^2}{3\Delta}. \]

The triangular interpolation kernel gives the time-averaged one-sided spectrum \(S(f)=A^2\operatorname{sinc}^4(f\Delta)\), with normalized sinc. Its integral defines equivalent noise bandwidth \(B=1/(3\Delta)\). The previous mapping \(\Delta=1/(2NEB)\) supplied only \(2NEB/3\), despite advertising NEB. The repaired mapping is \(\Delta=\max(h,1/(3NEB))\). An explicit source TSTEP retains its interval and grid-variance convention.

Eight independent seeds, 524288 samples per seed at \(h=1/8192\) s, and NEB=64 Hz measure pooled variance 42.7041 before repair and 63.8564268 after repair against 64. At least 65536 independent knots give relative standard error below 0.6%; the predeclared 5% bound exceeds eight standard errors. The finite sample spacing adds less than 0.03% phase-sampling correction. A one-second discard removes the source's initial zero-to-first-knot ramp.

Welch estimates use 16384-point periodic Hann windows, half overlap, 63 segments per seed, and eight seeds. The approximate effective segment count is 477, giving relative standard error 4.6%. A 30% bound exceeds six standard errors. Frequency bins start at 1 Hz, avoiding the mean-removal/DC bin. Comparison is against the analytic sinc transfer, including its rolloff:

Frequency (Hz) Measured PSD / analytic PSD 1 0.994512 2 1.016064 4 0.969538 32 0.986290 64 1.009167 128 1.008245

Sampling at update knots has larger variance than time averaging. Eight seeds and 8192 knots each check the independent formula \(\sigma_y^2[2/3+1/(3K^2)]\) for \(K\) samples per update interval:

K Measured variance Expected variance 1 0.499915340 0.500000000 2 0.374781627 0.375000000 4 0.343502529 0.343750000 16 0.333731599 0.333984375

Each uses the same conservative 5% statistical bound. Tests also check the simulation-step floor and legacy direct-API neB=0 fallback against the exact explicit-interval forward stream. Global .NEB 0 now fails cleanly; it previously aborted with std::bad_optional_access when thermal noise was enabled.

docs.title: Active thermal amplitude
docs.text:
Two independent implementation defects remained after the earlier stored-source repair: transition-region amplitude depended on the preceding resistive state, and already scaled interpolation knots retained old amplitudes. In addition, the solver sampled thermal noise before selecting the current step's slope.

White sources now retain unit-ASD knots and multiply the current amplitude after interpolation. Tests change amplitude 1→3→0→3 at the same time: the same realization rescales immediately and returns exactly zero when disabled. Rescaling draws no new random value. Junction updates select all three amplitudes before applying a single Norton sample to the physical terminals.

The explicit classical model is \(S_I=4k_BT G\), using the piecewise resistive slope: \(1/R_0\) below the gap, \(I_c/(ICFCT\,\Delta V)\) in transition, and \(1/R_N\) above the gap. This extends equilibrium resistor noise locally; it is not a microscopic theory of biased quasiparticles or transition-region shot noise. The noise guide states its physical limits and branch-current trace meaning. No constants or deterministic device equations are changed.

Direct tests visit subgap→transition→normal→transition→subgap in both polarities. A prescribed-voltage circuit independently selects each expected slope from its analytic PWL voltage and the existing explicit voltage predictor. KCL extracts the applied Norton current as -(I(V1)+I(B1)); I(B1) alone excludes that internal parallel source. Both analysis modes and positive-ground, ground-negative and two-non-ground terminals are checked. The six cases have maximum absolute discrepancy 5.114e-13 A. The per-sample allowance is 1 ppm of the independent SI noise value plus 1e-14 A, covering the retained legacy Boltzmann constant's rounding and linear-solve roundoff. The reference uses the forward unit source only to recover the fixed seeded realization; expected temperature, conductance, voltage and terminal signs are independent.

Full-cycle timestep retry with thermal, current and phase noise must replay a fresh same-process run at the final step bit-for-bit. Invalid API intervals, temperatures/resistances and clean CLI failure are also covered. At T=0 this classical source vanishes; zero conductance also gives zero noise.

docs.title: Compatibility and verification
docs.text:
Noise::determine_sampling_interval adds a static public method without changing object layouts or existing signatures. Internal white interpolation state now stores unit-ASD values. Ordinary connected explicit-interval sources retain draw ordering; floating-point operation order can change last bits. A junction whose two terminals are ground now advances its thermal generator once per step too, which changes subsequent global-stream draws. Correcting NEB deliberately changes omitted-interval and automatic thermal seeded waveforms. Changes in timestep, sampling or solver retry may also change noise timing; cross-build bit-identical output is not promised. The default NEB remains the existing 1 THz; stale 1 GHz documentation is corrected.

ctest --test-dir build/dev -R 'regression::(noise|cli|installed_package)' \
  --output-on-failure --no-tests=error

GCC16/Clang23 Debug and Release pass all 33 CTest groups. The complete ASan/UBSan suite with leak detection passes 33/33 in 198.80 s. All ten native binary/default/shared-library jobs pass for 078f091a1f53a25947134b5f39cff5e336b2176c in CI 42268024783. Exact red decks, binary hashes and failed assertions are preserved under build/audit-resolution/stochastic/. Compact green measurements, source hashes and qualification receipts are under artifacts/audit-resolution/white-thermal-noise/. The native group also checks the new method from a fresh installed-library consumer.

docs.title: Minimum build-tool qualification — 7 November 2026
docs.text:
The supported workflow requires CMake/CTest 3.21 or newer. Qualification owners consume CTest's JUnit output; declaring 3.14 while requiring a newer test workflow gave an inconsistent build contract. CMakeLists.txt now declares 3.21, matching the development and release instructions.

An isolated, task-owned PyPI installation of exactly CMake/CTest 3.21.0 configures and compiles the current candidate with local GNU 16.2.1 and Ninja. All 35/35 declared CTest groups pass, including an installed library moved to a path with spaces and a newly compiled external consumer. The current F27 candidate is included. The total configure/build/test campaign takes 27.59 s; this duration is verification provenance, not a performance benchmark.

The source remains C11/C++17. This build-tool decision changes no declared binary runtime baseline. It qualifies the local default-library workflow; native platform/library configurations and older OS/runtime checks have their own gates. It does not assert every old CMake/compiler/OS combination works.

artifacts/audit-resolution/cmake-min/ retains exact commands, source/owner identities, the candidate patch, install metadata and test inventory/JUnit. qualify_minimum.py reproduces the task-owned campaign from the repository root with its recorded 3.21.0 environment and prepared dependency cache. No global CMake installation was changed. An earlier attempt requested 3.21.7, which has no PyPI distribution; that diagnostic is retained, and is not a passing check.

docs.title: First-party coverage and risk review — 7 November 2026
docs.text: The current local campaign passes 35/35 complete CTest groups and measures 81.30% line, 88.95% function and 78.80% branch coverage with Clang/LLVM 23.1.4. Initial coverage was 57.54%/72.81%/52.47%. These figures include every compiled first-party source/header mapping; no first-party exclusion was added. Coverage supports the independent numerical studies, rather than proving their scientific correctness by itself. Native CI acceptance is recorded separately.

docs.title: Scope and measurement integrity
docs.text:
tools/coverage.py owns configuration, instrumentation, the full suite, profile merge, LLVM JSON, annotated HTML and per-module summaries. It inventories all src/*.cpp and include/JoSIM/*.hpp, including files with no compiled mapping. Only vendored solvers, vendored include/spline.h, generated code and test implementation are excluded. Solvers remain instrumented in sanitizer runs. Declarations, disabled preprocessor paths and uninstantiated templates do not acquire executable counters; they are not silently reported as covered.

The shared CTest validator requires exact declared/executed inventories, unique names, all twelve required regression groups and no skipped/failed cases. Release, library and coverage owners use the same contract. Tool-regression methods test false-success cases, stale data and coverage/mapping failures. Public-download contracts later extend the same qualification group. The first Windows run exposed native separators in the report inventory; paths are now canonical / names. All eight guard methods pass on the supplied native Windows host with Python 3.12.10. The full CI rerun remains a separate gate.

LLVM 23 reports 48 unused zero-hash mappings, representing 31 unique inline functions. The owner retains the diagnostics and verifies every live profile record against the exact exported execution count. Nonzero-hash mismatches, missing live records, count disagreements or unclassified warnings fail the campaign. Dense/sparse merging was independently checked to preserve totals. One reporting attempt incorrectly combined LLVM's debug output with JSON; its failed evidence remains. The corrected owner separates those passes.

docs.title: Requirements set before the current measurement
docs.text:
• Overall: at least 75% lines, 80% functions and 60% branches.
  • Eleven critical implementation owners: at least 80% lines and 65% branches.
  • Review uncovered critical decisions; percentages alone do not close a gap.
  • Preserve all first-party mappings and reject incomplete/skipped test runs.

The first expanded campaign reached only 73.77% lines. It was not accepted by lowering the requirement. Meaningful additions cover PWS/EXP closed forms, piecewise invalid grids, malformed sparse arrays, control-block parsing, sanity counts, file-format data/units, and the linear networks below. The piecewise work exposed F27, which was repaired before accepting the later campaign.

The reviewed policy also detects a drop exceeding 0.5 percentage point overall or 2 points in a critical module from the accepted reference. The smaller-module allowance accounts for a few source/counter changes; the independent floors still apply. References are specific to an LLVM major. An unreviewed major fails until its report and risk assessment are accepted; the tool never generates a passing reference from its own result.

tools/check_coverage.py also checks the current source hash, complete file/test inventories, mapping validation, counter arithmetic and module/overall agreement. tools/coverage-policy.json records the reviewed limits. The native release workflow requires the coverage job as well as its binary/library/utility jobs.

docs.title: High-risk additions
docs.text:
• Lossless matched line: 36 cases, two modes, two exact-grid timesteps and all grounded/reversed/floating port combinations. Matched source/load impedances imply half-amplitude input and an 8 ps delayed output with no reflected wave. Voltage error is below 2 nV; currents satisfy the 50 Ω port laws within 0.1 nA. Measured maximum voltage error is about 3.51e-17 V.
  • Controlled sources: 72 E/G/F/H cases, both modes and nine port combinations. Independent voltage/current gain laws and the 1 kΩ load establish signed transfer and current. Bounds are 2 ppm plus 0.1 nV, allowing six-digit output formatting; measured maximum voltage error is about 3.59e-15 V.
  • Capacitor orientation: 12 reversed/floating RC cases in both modes at two timesteps. The analytic ramp response, KCL and refinement protect history and sign handling. The conservative voltage envelope is 2*(a*tau)*(h/tau)^2 + 1 nV; halving the step must reduce error below 40% of its previous value plus the output-rounding allowance.

These supplement the existing analytic RLC, junction/buffer/phase/startup, thermal/colored-noise, SQUID and model-IV studies. They do not establish every SPICE dialect or every physical parameter regime.

docs.title: Remaining gaps and assessed limits
docs.text:
Area Remaining counters Assessment Solver resources KLU defaults/analysis allocation failures, some refactor/solve failures and bad_alloc Checked allocation results and RAII are reviewed; repeated singular/invalid-state recovery and leak checks execute cleanup. Tests do not induce host OOM or claim recovery from an OS kill. Mode/topology guards Final enum alternatives, short-circuit combinations and singular ground-to-ground source fallbacks Constructor/index invariants are reviewed. Both modes and valid grounded/reversed/floating numerical paths are exercised; zero branch counts can describe correlated predicates, not an unexecuted statement. Source/model edges Some diagnostic aliases, verbosity warnings, custom-file fallback and exact analytic-limit guards Main accepted/domain-error paths have independent tests. Standard-library function wrappers, impossible enum states and exact floating-point limit predicates are reviewed without claiming every diagnostic spelling is executed. Legacy subcircuit helpers Some four-node/JJ token substitutions and pre-parsed-model fallback paths Retained compatibility helpers are inspected against constructor token positions; common legacy binding and the supported parameter-aware path are tested. These counters stay visible; no universal compatibility claim is made. Formatting and public helpers Some progress/verbosity variants, empty manually populated traces and unused getters/hooks Data/units and destination failures are checked for CSV/DAT/RAW/stdout; progress has separate timing and worker-lifetime evidence. Direct public-container mutation must preserve the documented API invariants.

The raw branch inventory retains exact locations/counts. It includes individual short-circuit predicates; several can share one source line. Remaining cases are retained limitations or reviewed guard/helper variants, not excluded code. No unexplained high-risk integration, history, noise or repaired-defect path is being accepted on a smoke-test result alone.

docs.title: Reproduction and evidence
docs.text:
From the repository root, use matching Clang, llvm-cov and llvm-profdata majors:

python3 -B tools/coverage.py --build-dir build/coverage --output artifacts/coverage
python3 -B tools/check_coverage.py --summary artifacts/coverage/summary.json \
  --output artifacts/coverage/policy.json

Use fresh campaign paths. --initial-cache can reuse verified dependency sources. CI selects matching Ubuntu Clang/LLVM 18 tools explicitly. Its initial 35-group report passes the same risk floors and mapping checks, with 81.32%/88.95%/78.77% overall coverage. The reviewed major-18 reference uses the two-decimal values published in CI42307801289; exact counters remain in its machine-readable artifact. A subsequent native/guard run is still required. A report from another source tree cannot pass the current-source guard merely because its percentages are high.

artifacts/audit-resolution/coverage-policy/ retains exact commands, source/tool identities, all module counters, mapping validation, test inventories/JUnit, annotated HTML, the policy decision, numerical receipts and exact owners. Earlier campaigns remain separate, including the missed target and failed JSON reporting witness. Final integrated/source-version/native checks remain required.

docs.title: Manual, package version and migration — 7 November 2026
docs.text: The source version is 3.0.0. The public C++ layouts changed in Input, Netlist/Subcircuit, Results/Simulation, PhaseSource, RelevantTrace and ProgressBar. The existing CMake package policy is SameMajorVersion; a major version change makes that boundary explicit. Consumers request major 3 and recompile against matching headers/libraries. Unix shared libraries carry SOVERSION 3; the local shared object reports SONAME libjosim.so.3. The historical v2.7 tag is retained. This document is a preparation record, not a claim that release/Pages publication or the final integrated-source gates have completed.

docs.title: Manual and examples
docs.text:
The README, English and Japanese manuals now describe the actual build commands, KLU-only support, retired parallel/solver switches, source/model validation, noise bandwidth, fixed-step/full-restart mechanism and public API migration. The Japanese pages link current English model/scientific guides; they do not claim to translate every new study. Obsolete Azure/testing-branch badges, versioned setup instructions, unqualified 10 ms timing and a broken duplicate plotting implementation are removed. Exponential signs/default tables and unreferenced footnotes/links are corrected. Existing scientific references and historical release entries remain.

The English/Japanese JTL netlists are identical and run in both analysis modes:

  • 4,000 finite samples at 0.25 ps over the declared 1 ns interval.
  • Each triangular input integrates to 0.9999957293 Phi0, within the predeclared 10 ppm allowance for its rounded 827.13 µV amplitude.
  • Each of the two junctions advances by one 2π phase increment per input pulse. Maximum deviation is about 1.24e-5 rad, below 1e-4 rad including finite settling and six-digit CSV rounding. Both modes agree on those printed increments.
