These invariants check the example's intended pulse transport; copied output is not used as an independent physical reference. The current example CSV excerpt is regenerated. The README/index quickstart uses the existing sink example, which has no incidental model-IV output. Its 4,000 output samples are finite. The maintained plotting command creates an actual self-contained HTML export. Earlier terminal/plot images remain labelled illustrations where applicable.

docs.title: Site checks and local context
docs.text:
An isolated Python 3.12 environment installs pinned MkDocs 1.6.1 and Material 9.8.0. The strict build and the local HTML file/fragment checker pass. The initial 52-page build exposed ten broken links/anchors; none is suppressed. The checker also rejects missing assets/fragments and a generated context/ directory in controlled fixtures. The final inventory and exact counts are in links.json.

mkdocs.yml explicitly excludes ignored local docs/context/ notes. Package installation now includes the public manual and also excludes that directory; installed-consumer checks require linked migration/model/sweep/performance guides and reject installed local context. Before the repair, all four guides were absent from the installed payload (F30).

The old polyfill.io script is removed and MathJax is pinned to 3.2.2, following its modern-browser guidance. The generated syntax page renders 382 MathJax containers with no math-error elements or browser console errors/warnings. The Japanese home page visibly shows 3.0.0, C++17/C11, CMake 3.21 and the supported/retired choices. These are local browser checks; the deployed site still requires separate verification.

docs.title: Build and API checks
docs.text:
Local package/version qualification uses exact CMake/CTest 3.21.0 and fresh installed consumers requesting josim 3.0. Default and shared library-mode qualification includes every declared CTest group and installation relocation. Current receipts record the source revision plus working-tree identity; final clean-source/native checks remain separate.

The help menu also advertised --sanitycheck and --Verbose=1, although both failed with unknown-switch status 255 (F29). It now prints accepted lowercase --sanity and --verbose. A process regression extracts all eight advertised long options and executes every one successfully. It does not broaden parsing or revive the retired switches. CLI and fresh-consumer checks pass 2/2.

Evidence is retained in artifacts/audit-resolution/documentation/ (dependency report, strict build, checker fixtures, browser observations, actual example commands/data and old help/package failures), cmake-min-3-final/ (minimum tools) and library-3-final/ (default/shared modes). Those machine-readable receipts provide exact source/tool/configuration identities and executed test results.

docs.title: Piecewise waveform grids — 7 November 2026
docs.text:
Coverage-driven source tests exposed F27: a negative first PWL/PWS time was accepted with a warning, then time zero was prepended ahead of it. The stored grid was therefore unordered. Both public sources share Function::parse_pwl.

The bounded CLI witness uses points (-1 ps, 1 V) and (2 ps, 2 V), 30 ordinary samples and a 1 kΩ load. Both old commands return success. PWS returns 1 V at time zero, then 1.296632 V at 0.1 ps. An ordered half-cosine segment would give 1 + (1-cos(pi/3))/2 = 1.25 V at zero. The prepend/clamp combination introduces the discontinuity; this is independent of circuit integration.

Negative first times are now rejected. The maintained syntax uses finite, nonnegative, strictly increasing times and finite signed amplitudes. A positive first time still prepends zero with the same amplitude and a warning. This preserves valid delayed-start behavior without introducing pre-zero waveform control. INVALID_PWL_PARAMETERS is appended to the existing error enum; existing values, signatures and class layouts remain unchanged.

Direct source tests cover both aliases, incomplete pairs, duplicate/decreasing times, negative first times and unresolved/non-finite time/value data. Valid PWS endpoints/nonuniform segments and EXP rise/fall use independent closed forms. CLI regressions require useful failure status/diagnostics and no output file.

All four local GCC/Clang Debug/Release configurations pass 35/35 CTest groups. Full Clang Debug ASan/UBSan with leak detection passes 35/35 in 212.87 s. The focused source/parser/numerical/library/tool groups also pass 5/5. Final integrated/native qualification remains a separate requirement.

artifacts/audit-resolution/piecewise-negative/ retains the actual old decks, CSV/log witnesses, commands, source hashes and compiler/sanitizer receipts. test/function_regression.cpp and test/regression_cli.py protect the repair.

docs.title: Public download verification — preparation, 7 November 2026
docs.text:
The 3.0.0 candidate at 5a27110 passes all twelve native/library/utility/coverage CI jobs (run42314611144). This preparation adds a documentation prerequisite and postpublication verification. Actual public 3.0.0 downloads and execution remain pending the final source gates, permitted integration, tag and publication.

tools/verify_release.py resolves the public tag to the expected full commit, requires a published stable release, and downloads the real archive, checksum and sidecar manifest. It checks API size/digest where provided, the sidecar hash, embedded-manifest agreement, source/version/target/clean identity, exact payload inventory and every payload size/hash. Extraction rejects escaping paths, links, special files and duplicate names; packaged local project context is rejected.

Native execution checks the host/architecture and CLI source/version banner, then runs the CLI regressions and independent numerical suite against the actual downloaded binary. Empty, skipped or failed runs and incomplete/wrong-binary numerical reports fail. Source/test-owner and executable identities are checked and recorded. JSON and readable receipts distinguish prepared downloads from passed native execution.

The reusable verify-release.yml runs five targets. Linux downloads on a modern host and executes in the same pinned legacy userspace used for package builds, with network disabled. Windows and both macOS architectures use native runners. The tagged publisher invokes this workflow after upload. Manual dispatch accepts a public tag/full commit and records the verification source separately. Asset HTTP requests are anonymous; the optional CI read token is used only for metadata.

The publisher now uses reviewed versioned notes and disables asset overwrites. The documentation prerequisite builds the pinned manual in strict mode and checks every local file/fragment plus the context exclusion. Branch builds do not publish a release or claim that postpublication tests have run.

docs.title: Windows archive-name follow-up
docs.text:
The first 9ae6f0a Windows CI run passed 34/35 groups but failed the new archive fixture: ZipInfo changed bin\escape to bin/escape before the asserted rejection. The fixture therefore did not contain its intended raw name on Windows. The reader also exposes the original stored name separately.

The fixture now writes the literal header name, and the verifier checks orig_filename before normalization. The same unsafe bytes are rejected with both native and Windows-normalizing readers; no assertion or path rule is relaxed. All thirteen guard methods pass on native x870-win10/Python 3.12.10 in 0.547 s and in all five local compiler/sanitizer test configurations. Native PowerShell parsing also accepts the workflow's 4 PowerShell blocks; it does not execute release commands. public-download-preparation/windows/ retains old/new normalization witnesses, CI failure scope and native source/hash receipts.

Before this tooling-only repair, the unchanged first-party C++ source passes four fresh local 35-group configurations, full ASan/UBSan/leaks 35/35 in 216.85 s, the reviewed 45 static-warning locations, and coverage requirements at 82.43%/89.23%/79.38% line/function/branch. Final native/integrated qualification of the corrected verifier remains required.

docs.title: Pulse domains and large cycle counts — 7 November 2026
docs.text:
F28 is a source evaluation defect. return_pulse converted (t-TD)/PER to int64_t without checking the domain or range. A zero period returned success in Release and triggered UBSan's floating-to-integer diagnostic. A valid finite period can also exceed the integer cycle-count range.

The finite witness uses h=2^-40 s, PER=2^-104 s, PW=PER/2, zero delay and instantaneous edges, a 1 V source and a 1 kΩ load. Its eight sample times are exact multiples of PER: every sampled source value must be 1 V. The old Release binary instead produced [1,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]; UBSan stopped at cycle count 2^64. This deliberately aliases the source and tests defined evaluation at represented times. It does not establish adequate sampling of such a high-frequency pulse.

docs.title: Repair and compatibility
docs.text:
Parsing now requires finite amplitudes, finite nonnegative TD/TR/TF/PW and a finite strictly positive PER, with at most seven arguments. Validation does not depend on verbosity. Zero rise/fall times remain valid instantaneous edges; zero plateau duration remains a valid triangular pulse. The old zero-width "redundant" warning was inaccurate and is no longer emitted. Reparsing replaces the stored pulse rather than appending to its previous data.

For ordinary cycle counts, the existing arithmetic and operation order remain. At or beyond 2^63, including an overflowing floating quotient, evaluation uses fmod(t-TD, PER) without an integer cast. No public signature or class layout changes. INVALID_PULSE_PARAMETERS is appended to the error enum, preserving existing numeric values and the old diagnostic enum names for callers.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Direct source tests use independent endpoint tables for rise, plateau, fall, delay, period wrapping, defaults, inverted pulses, instantaneous edges and zero plateaus. Exact dyadic large times cover both integer-range and quotient overflow. Invalid definitions are checked at both verbosity levels. Process regressions exercise both analysis modes, clean rejection without output, and all eight expected values of the finite witness within 1 nV.

All four local GCC/Clang Debug/Release configurations pass 35/35 CTest groups. The changed source passes the existing focused Clang-Tidy checks with no warnings. Full Clang Debug ASan/UBSan with leak detection passes 35/35 in 223.26 s. Native CI remains a separate gate.

The performance acceptance was declared before timing: seven counterbalanced pairs on a 64-cell pulse/resistor bank, 300,000 steps, both analysis modes, identical CSV bytes and no more than 5% median wall-time regression. Independent 0/1 mV point values must agree within 1 nV. The observed median increases are 1.28% in voltage mode and 0.41% in phase mode, with identical CSVs and no changed numerical tolerance. Other heavy local jobs were stopped during timing.

artifacts/audit-resolution/pulse-domain/ retains old/new witnesses, commands, binary/source/owner hashes, all compiler receipts, the exact timing owner and predeclared acceptance. The baseline is clean 00512b6; local repair receipts identify 7100a39 plus the source diff. An initial timing-owner path typo failed before executing any benchmark and is retained under build/; it is not a pass.

docs.text: The initial audit ran Clang-Tidy on Input, Netlist, RelevantTrace, Output, Simulation, IV, Function, Noise and Rng. The rerun adds Inductor after F25. Checks cover Clang's analyzers, integer division, suspicious semicolons, use-after-move and unchecked optional access. docs.title: Invariants and their limits
docs.text:
• Every concrete component assigns currentIndex_ = bi++ before node/stamp setup. BasicComponent::set_node_indices fills exactly the optional node indices selected by NodeConfig; the corresponding simulation branches use those same topologies. F25's component tests exercise all four configurations; numerical/noise/source tests exercise both modes and orientations.
  • Retained-result accesses in Simulation are immediately guarded by the same vector optional. No intervening mutation occurs between the guard and access.
  • Model-IV generation builds a single-junction testbench without explicit trace selection. Simulation engages every result unknown, including its first node. IV::do_simulate is scoped to this generated testbench, as the API guide states. It is not a general arbitrary-matrix measurement API.

The public component/index containers remain mutable for compatibility. Direct callers must preserve their constructor invariants; arbitrary corruption of component fields is outside the supported embedding contract. Sparse-array dimensions/indices and solved finite values receive separate runtime checks.

This is a focused review of high-risk owners, not exhaustive static proof. Compiler warnings and executed sanitizer/numerical tests provide separate evidence. Passing an optional-access review does not establish physical accuracy.

initial-dispositions.json maps all 49 original locations; current/dispositions.json maps all 45 current locations. review-summary.json records identities, counts and limits. The current raw reports retain warnings so future reviewers can inspect the evidence directly.

docs.title: Quantitative scientific evidence
docs.text:
Individual studies version the equations, independent references, tolerances and commands. Selected measured results:

  • Linear circuits: 36 RC/RL/RLC cases; maximum finest-step voltage errors 13.1534/13.1534/14.0995 nV, KVL <= 5.00001e-10 V, KCL zero at CSV precision, error decreases 3.4–4x on step halving. Additional matched-line 36, controlled-source 72 and reversed/floating-capacitor 12 cases protect signs/delays and conservation.
  • RSJ: period errors 567.504/142.585/35.6945 ppm under refinement; mean pulse area agrees with SI Phi0 within 0.092 ppm over 820–821 rotations. Phase study uses an independent 70-digit prediction for long-run drift.
  • Buffer: tightened Radau and independent BDF agree within 2.05e-10 scaled state units (1e-8 budget). Finest-step waveform errors 19.1501/40.5556 nV reverse/forward. Pulse-area allowance 5e-6 Phi0; reverse net response -1.38349e-6 Phi0 and forward 0.999997568 Phi0.
  • Thermal/white: interpolation gives NEB = 1/(3B); six state-dependent circuit checks have maximum 5.114e-13 A discrepancy against independently computed SI amplitudes (1 ppm + 1e-14 A bound). Classical S_I=4kBTG is the stated physical approximation.
  • Colored noise: pole-bank/sample-gain corrections checked across 48 banks and controlled seeds, with declared variance/PSD budgets. Delay/tick/retry and flux/current units are independently tested.
  • SQUID: finite-loop flux residual <= 3.713e-9 Phi0 (5e-7 budget); 16 seeds at each of three NEBs yield PSD/reference ratios 1.020164/0.998104/0.992709, inside family 99% intervals plus 5% model allowance. Halving timestep/output spacing changes PSD <= 0.1413%/0.0612%.
  • Storage: 112 paired controlled runs retain identical CSVs. Noise peak RSS 102.77→89.45 MiB; 32-voltage bank 199.77→159.49 MiB. Borrowed views and progress record separately controlled time/CPU reductions and unaffected-case bounds. These are workload-specific measurements.

docs.title: Compatibility and remaining boundaries
docs.text:
Version 3 is justified by changed public C++ layouts. Recompile with matching headers/libraries and compatible toolchains; Unix shared objects carry ABI 3 and CMake selection uses SameMajorVersion. CSV/DAT/RAW conventions and supported KLU ownership remain documented. Migration details intentional corrected behaviour and retired options.

Linux x64 claims glibc 2.12 and ARM64 glibc 2.17. Legacy userspaces execute on modern kernels; this does not qualify original RHEL kernels. Windows uses the static MSVC runtime. Apple Silicon/Intel deployment targets remain 11.0/10.15, while CI executes its actual current runner OS; metadata does not establish every older macOS release.

Each attempt uses a fixed step; smaller-step failure recovery restarts the whole run. No conventional adaptive error-control/Newton guarantee is added. Check timestep, settling and output sampling for each model. Noise replay requires matching build/seed/effective sampling. Global RNG ownership permits sequential runs on one designated thread; use process parallelism. Decimation does not reduce stored internal histories, whose double payload scales as 8N(1+retained unknowns+requested applied-current histories).

The bounded analytic/stochastic/model studies resolve the audited supported behaviours. They do not establish every SPICE dialect, arbitrary public-container mutation, every physical regime, quantum noise, original undocumented screenshots or a nonlinear-inductor solver.

docs.title: JoSIM 3.0.0
docs.text:
This release consolidates the public branches and original noise research, repairs the audited simulator and library defects, and updates the maintained builds, tools and documentation. JoSIM remains freely available under MIT.

Recompile C++ applications with matching 3.0.0 headers and libraries. Public type layouts changed. CMake package selection now uses major 3; shared Unix libraries carry ABI version 3. Existing v2.7 remains unchanged.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• Repair hierarchical parameters/models, pin aliases, requested traces and startup/phase histories. Reject malformed input and failed output explicitly.
  • Correct seeded replay, white/colored-noise normalization and state-dependent thermal noise. Add controlled gate, flux and critical-current noise workflows.
  • Rebuild device histories per model-IV point and preserve bias through retries. Add explicit sweep timing, a safe external circuit-sweep owner and tested examples.
  • Add analytic linear-network, junction, buffer, phase, stochastic and conservation regressions. Protect first-party coverage and complete qualification inventories.
  • Make supported embedding failures recoverable, qualify relocated installed consumers, and retire nonfunctional SuperLU/parallel options explicitly.
  • Reduce avoidable history allocation, per-step copies and progress polling. Controlled studies show 13–20% lower peak memory and 15–21% lower wall time in selected workloads; these are measured cases, not universal speed guarantees.
  • Refresh English/Japanese manuals, packaged guides, plotting utilities and build/release procedures. Fix PULSE cycle overflow and advertised CLI options.

The changelog and audit ledger give the full changes, independent expectations, tolerances and evidence.

docs.title: Model and workflow limits
docs.text: Each transient attempt uses a fixed step. A smaller-step retry restarts the whole run; this is not conventional adaptive error control. Validate timestep, settling and output sampling for your circuit. Noise replay requires the same build, seed and effective sampling settings. Model .iv is a finite single-JJ testbench, distinct from an arbitrary-circuit sweep. Capacitor IC=, a direct BETA_C= field and nonlinear inductors remain outside the supported model; documented preparation/conversion alternatives are provided.
